Having just played through Dying Light 2 for the first time in preparation for Dying Light: The Beast, I feel an urgent need to voice my disappointment with this entire experience. While I dislike comparing one work of art to another, when it comes to this game in particular, I find it easiest to voice my frustrations by just comparing it with its predecessor. Because for some reason, the developers of Dying Light 2 seemingly went by the mentality of "If it ain't broke, fix it anyway and make it worse and more video-gamey lol."

For starters, the story of this game is about as abysmal as the first game. That on its own isn't necessarily the biggest of deals; I don't intend to play a parkour-heavy, zombie slaughterfest for the deep story and characters. But whereas the first game tried its damn hardest to keep the story in the background, with only a few important characters sprinkled throughout, its sequel goes for a much more ever-present, branching-decision-heavy, morally grey, and in-your-face story that I sincerely couldn't care less for. The level of writing present in this game is sub-par, the characters all feel like parodies of themselves, and there isn't a single memorable character anywhere in this game. Yet the game is also about two times as long as the OG, with way too many shallow characters sharing the limelight for me to care about any of them. Mix that in with a story that is somehow even more reliant on contrivances and that much of it feels blatantly unfinished, and I have to be completely honest in saying that DL2 is one of the few games where I actively started skipping through cutscenes because of how little I cared for what was going on.

When it comes to the parkour, which is one of the most important parts of these games, I could talk about all the weird changes forever. How it feels too floaty, how it isn't as blood-pumping when there aren't as many enemies present, how sometimes the game just refuses to listen to inputs or gets you stuck on nothing, how awful the tower mini-games are, with you actively having to wait for moving parts in this fast-paced game, killing any semblance of pacing, etc. I could also talk about the fact that after I finished the game and put 30+ hours into it, I actually found the late-game parkour to be more satisfying than the first game's, yet by that time it was too little too late to hook me back in. Even literally perfect systems, like the fact that in the first game your character would only climb over an obstacle if you HELD DOWN the jump button, were changed for no reason, with Aiden climbing up obstacles even when you don't want him to.

And then there's just everything else... The combat has no sense of progression, because whether you're holding a regular, level 1 common pipe or a level 6 legendary bat makes no difference, with you usually having to just hit a zombie 3~4 times and then pressing the funny F button to kill it on the spot (unless it's a zombie whose level is too high for that, because hooray for level scaling emirite?). The zombies themselves are far too predictable in how they react to you, your movement, and your attacks. Your consumables, clothes, and even some equipment are tied to levels and rarity now, which leads to about as many awesome feelings of progression (making your glider faster) as it does purely pointless moments (+0.3% parkour XP from your gloves). Speaking of parkour XP... The rate at which you get XP has been drastically nerfed from the first game, with you now getting most of it for completing quests. This feels like such a gross regression of what was a completely fine system that incentivised you to try fun and awesome parkour routes at every opportunity. And I could just keep going...

4/10

review:
Can't recommend the game overall due to so many issues adding up. 
First off, there are a lot of frustrating bugs with the movement and collision/geometry. You'll get caught on invisible objects, get stuck in animation loops, run into UI bugs, and sometimes just soft lock the game and need to exit. 
The next biggest issue is the story and dialogue; the characters and main story are not developed well at all which feels extra bad given how much characters talk. The pacing is pretty bad where you can go all the way to the last hour of the game and see barely any development of the main plot. It spends so much time trying to build the world but it ends up feeling shallow because the characters aren't developed well.
The last issue to bring up is the core gameplay. There are a lot of gripes I have with the gameplay but the biggest ones are with the weapon progression, the looting and item crafting being too grindy and bloated, and change in night time dynamics from the first game. The game really tries to shove in live service elements with dailies and weeklies and it ends up hindering the progression to the guns. The first game had you reach firearms pretty fast and intermix them with your melee attacks but in this game, because it's locked behind a grind you can end up finishing the game without utilizing guns. It sucks because the survival setting of the game elevates the desire for guns as the goal to reach for but hinders your progression so much it just hurts to get there. The other gameplay gripe is the night time dynamics. Again looking back at the first game, in order to navigate the night the game encouraged staying above ground level with your parkour to avoid confrontation with a specific powerful enemy type that will chase you if caught. This was great because you had to think about your routes and puzzle out your parkour as well as get a thrill from evading these enemies. You would get caught from time to time and get chased but that was alright. But for some reason, this sequel shoves too many of these enemies both on the ground level and the rooftops. This is a confusing and frustrating change because all it encourages now is to just run past them or initiating the chase anyway and escaping. It becomes really tedious and it hurts the risk/reward decision making when choosing to navigate during day or night because you just end up choosing day time as much as possible. The last big gameplay gripe to talk about is with the looting and crafting. These gameplay elements are so bloated, there are way too many items to pick up and items to utilize. There are only so many active use slots too, so it ends up being too much of a hassle to maintain all these items. What ends up happening is that you end up blowing through the game sticking to only a few items because it's too unwieldy to craft, equip, and maintain.
I will also note that the co-op experience for the main story is also bad. There were bugs so bad that they would break the lobby and force remaking them. And because there's so much dialogue and contextual actions, the already bad pacing just gets worse due to needing to wait every single time for everyone to be present do those actions.
I felt that the first game was the better experience (but not by too much) with it's better progression. And when you hit those smooth moments with the parkour it can scratch that Mirror's Edge itch that so few current games do. However, there are just too many issues with the game to give a good recommendation.

TLDR:

Review:

Dying Light 2 is a game I had long been curious about, but never tried when it first released due to the very mixed reviews it received. However, when it went on sale, I decided to give it a chance despite my strong skepticism, particularly after Tencent acquired a majority share of Techland. That influence quickly became visible, as the game soon introduced a store where cosmetic items and weapons could be purchased—items that directly affect the gameplay experience. Even though it is a single player game and technically impacts no one but the player, I still find this to be a disappointing direction. In my view, it downgrades the overall package from being slightly above average to merely average, if not a bit below.

Setting corporate decisions aside, how is the game itself?

The game is good and successfully builds on many of the strengths that made Dying Light 1 enjoyable. However, I feel its open world has grown too large, with too much focus on repetitive activities rather than being compact and unique. The parkour system works very well, and the world is designed to support it effectively. You begin with limited movement and gradually evolve into a parkour expert, turning the environment into your playground. Enemies feel more dangerous this time around. While there are not many new types, those that exist are slightly more threatening than in the first game, and the few new additions stand out and make the world more engaging.

The story itself is rather simple and, in my opinion, a bit too short. Throughout the game, you are forced to make choices that, based on my playthroughs, seemed to have tangible consequences on how the ending played out. The narrative is left fairly open, with several questions unanswered, which creates a desire to continue following Aiden’s journey. There are plenty of side quests, many of which are interesting and often involve multiple steps, giving them a sense of uniqueness. The quality of these quests was generally solid, though not exceptional. Personally, I grew tired of them over time, as the NPCs tend to talk excessively. This can sometimes be immersive, but for me it became too much conversation and too little gameplay.

Missions constantly bug out—objectives don’t update, forcing you to restart the game and replay the mission. In co-op, the animations are horrendous and completely break immersion.

They “fixed” ragdolls, but the physics are still clunky, stiff, and filled with repetitive animations. Ropes in co-op are also glitched—you often have to wait several seconds before you can use one if your friend has just used it.

I was hyped when they added guns, but the grind kills the excitement. You have to slog through painfully long, repetitive, and boring missions just to get weapons and ammo. And when missions glitch like I said before, you’re forced to redo the entire thing from scratch.

I was genuinely looking forward to an expansion, but instead, we got nothing. Now, if you want that “OG Dying Light” experience, you’re expected to buy a completely new game.

The only positive thing I can mention is the gore update they added—it’s actually well done and a fun addition. For a moment, it almost distracts you from the terrible ragdoll physics and repetitive combat animations.


If you've played and liked DL1 you can and should skip this!

review:
I really REALLY hate this game! It stands for everything that is wrong with triple AAA singleplayer gaming. Everything is bloated as hell with convoluted systems, that are ment to keep the players playing forever. Instead of just developing a game that just ends at a certain point, this game never shuts up, like ever! NPCs talk for hours, loot never stops, infinite amount of challenges, stupid weapon upgrade systems, a lockpick minigame from Skyrim, Ubisoft like towers to unfog the map, it is just exhausting to play this game.
Every dumb mechanic you could possibly imagine is in this game. The most jarring thing tho is, it all comes over 10 WHOLE YEARS TOO LATE! Techland missed any change in the industry over a decade and comes with this game around the corner in 2022. These guys lived under a rock for 10 years and pretend this is some masterpiece you play forever.

But a bit more in detail:

First of, Dying Light 2 doesnt respect your time in the slightest. Everything is blowted as hell. This worst thing in this game by far is the progression system. To level up my health or stamina, i have to find three inhibitors, so far so good, but to unlock a certain skill, i have to have a certain amount of points into health or stamina. For example, wallrunning can only be unlocked by having 220 points in stamina, so i have to level up stamina with an inhibitor to 220 but then i cannot unlock wallrunning right away, i have to level up my characters level to unlock a skill point and i do that, by running around doing parkour stuff, or doing sidequest, after that i unlock the mentioned skill point that i can now use in my skill tree to unlock wallrunning, BUT only if i have those 220 points in stamina through the inhibitors. 
Its such a convoluted system and unnessary so. There are so many layers which takes forever to unlock.

Next is the equipment you have. So you wanna level up your medpacks so you can faster heal or having more efficient molotovs? For that you have to loot a lot of stuff, i mean A LOT, and collect zombie trophies, the higher the level, the better the zombie trophy has to be. So you could just run around and kill zombie and loot everything, but no not every zombie drops a trophy so you have to kill a million zombies to collect these trophies, its annoying as hell and remember, all this for just a medipack upgrade...

Everything in this game is designed to rob your lifetime and engage with 10 year old systems that are not fun.

And looting takes forever in this game, you have to hold, mash or press a button for every single crate you open and after that press a button again to pick the loot up, because of course everything will be picked up individually and not all that once and of course there is an animation for everything, which really kills the flow of the game and steals even more of your lifetime.

The movement ranges from ok, to absolutly aweful. Sometimes Aiden doesnt grab a ledge, he feels floaty or doenst do what you want, or the systems doesnt work at all.
Even in the movement department the game cant stop to annoy you. The most basic things that you can do in a free running system are locked here and you have grind for them. Wanna do a wall to wall jump? Hell no! First collect those inhibitors and then level up your character, before you can do a wall jump hahaha funny! 
Which means, movement in the first 15 hours or so, is not fun, same for the battle system. 
Imagine Mirrors Edge locking every move behind an upgrade, that would be the worst system ever but Dying Light 2 does excatly that!

It took me 20 hours, 20 goddamn hours, to unlock the grappling hook, why? Why does it take forever to unlock the most basic stuff in this game?! Ah yes, almost forgot, to steal your lifetime.

Story is just not it man. The dialouge ranges from ok to aweful. The story is just boring, full of cliches and not worth your time. Just skip it all, you will just look into faces all the time anyway, so why bother?! 

The only good thing about this abomination is the atmosphere at night and the soundesign is great. 
Zombies look good and sound awesome, slashing zombies is ok, but like i already said, the ok stuff takes way to long to get going. It doesnt respect your time, and every mechanic is annyoing in this.

Its one of the worst games i have ever played. This is a parody of a videogame, nothing else.

One last thing, just play Dead Island 2, at least that game has the decency to end after 15 to 20 hours. 
Still a cringe story, but fighting in this is atcual fun, and you get all the mechanis early. Ex devs of Free Radical know their stuff, Techland doesnt...

review:
Dying light 2 is without a doubt one of the worst games I have ever played. 

The gameplay is lacking, combat and parkour are a direct downgrade from dying light 1. The finisher moves for enemies were cool for the first few hours until you realize only 1-3 of them exist for each kind of weapon. (Only 4 types of weapons) This makes combat repetitive and boring almost immediately. The parkour is also a massive disappointment. It feels weightless and most of the new abilities are lacking or otherwise useless. The dropkick, which was a signature attack in Dying light 1 felt terrible to use in the game. The use of leveled armor felt lame and unnecessary, I didn't feel like it really enhanced my experience at all. I only used the gear that looked the best because I didn't notice any significant changes when trying new armor pieces. 

The characters are very boring and most of their behaviors make little to no sense. NO ONE is memorable at all, they all were written very poorly. Their moods range from hating you to loving you to hating you again at the drop of a hat. The dialogue options don't change anything about the characters and most of the time this game forces you to select all dialogue options in most conversations, rendering dialogue completely useless for character development and most parts of the story.

The story is terrible and lacks any kind of thinking. Most of your “choices” don't actually add up to anything. The game's entire story feels rushed. Mix this with the lobotomites that are the characters of this game and the story is complete trash. Also for some reason this game feels the need to add a cutscene for every door you open during a main quest and multiple for each boss fight, making a simple boss fight take an unreasonable amount of time. This game introduced a faction system to the dying light series. This system is the biggest nothing burger I have had the displeasure of eating. No matter which faction you pick, that side will always seem morally justified and the other side turns into a bunch of war mongering psychopaths. It's like they are afraid to let the player choose a side with complex choices and consequences. This makes the entire game's story feel like a waste of time and nothing matters. 

Also the amount of bugs in dying light 2 are insane. Quests not working, characters not spawning which stop you from obtaining a quest you need for a collectible, your character failing to grab a ledge or properly execute the parkour you are trying to perform. Enemies failing to spawn during a combat challenge which fails you instantly. These bugs waste your time and make the game far less enjoyable.

My friend and I decided to do a 100% completion of this game. Part of that involves obtaining every collectible in the base game. Many collectibles are locked behind quests that are easily missable making this task insufferable. We also had to get the worst achievement of all time (Ultramarathon). This requires you to run a combined 960,000 meters. This means not interacting with anything in the game other than running. No looting, ziplining, paragliding, or falling. Just running. Even when playing the game fully through, you will only get around 200k with a single playthrough while doing most side quests, effectively making this achievement the most grindy, time wasting piece of trash. This achievement is the cherry on top for the most atrocious game I've played in a while and it perfectly symbolizes what this game is all about, wasting your time making the experience as unenjoyable as possible. For anyone wanting to 100% this game, I'm advising you not to because it's a huge waste of your time. 

This is such a downgrade from Dying light 1. The first game had so much love and attention to detail put into it. The visual storytelling was incredible and the character’s motivations were reasonable and justified. The story and characters are memorable and believable. Dying light 1 was a simple story told very well and would implore anyone who has not played it to pick that game up whenever possible. Under no circumstances would I ever suggest anyone play Dying light 2, this game is a massive waste of time and a huge disappointment to the fans of the series.

 I'm giving this game a deserving 2/10. The only reason this game even gets a 2 is because it looks slightly better graphically than Dying light 1.

Simply in love with this game. There is zero rng apart from who goes first (player 2 is slightly favored 52/48). People say it's a card game/rts hybrid. Now you may ask, "wouldn't this get boring"? Well it sure would if there wasn't a catch. 

In each match there are the 11 base set units and a set of random units. Usually between 5 and 11 random units, depending on settings. This makes each match unique and you have to make up your strategy on the fly. There is also quite a large amount of single player content right now, with a lot more coming. The campaign and combat training together are a great tutorial. Once you are done with those you can fight bots of multiple difficulties or hop on to casual matches. 

There is also a great amount of material on the internet to make you a better player. https://prismatalibrary.blog/ https://prismata.gamepedia.com/Prismata_Wiki http://107.170.7.25/prismata/index.html

review:
[h1]Tornuffalo is a good cheapie to start your VR collection.[/h1]

Tornuffalo has one major feature that most VR games still do not have: IK arms.  Well, it has a single arm, anyway.  This feature is implemented so well that it's a selling point of getting this game.  For 99 cents, it's worth experiencing.  It's also replayable thanks to the arcade style score-driven gameplay.  That said, the gameplay is mostly just breaking gems and avoiding everything else.

This is a stationary game that requires roomscale, meaning that you don't get locomotion sickness from it, because the only way to move is to actually move your real body.  You can't, however, jump over obstacles.  You're limited to ducking, strafing left and right, and using your hammer to make objects go around or over you.

If you have a big playspace with a lot of room for error around your boundries, then pick this up as it's definitely worth its price tag. review:
Bad Dream: Coma is a fascinating point-and-click adventure that stands out for its depth and replayability. What makes it especially engaging is not just the multiple endings, but the fact that most puzzles can be solved in different ways depending on your prior choices. The game constantly reflects on your morality. Every action, whether kind or cruel, ripples outward and changes how the world reacts to you. Maybe the birds despise you, or maybe you prove yourself a true board game aficionado! Either way, nothing you do is without consequence.

The storyline is both surreal and heartbreaking. You explore a dreamscape shaped by the imagination of a child, yet it reflects the trauma of an adult man who lost his parents at a young age. The atmosphere can swing between twisted nightmare and peaceful fantasy depending on your decisions, making every playthrough feel unique.

Death itself even plays a role in the story, but he’s not exactly thrilled with your interference. In fact, he’s decided to stop taking souls altogether, leaving you with the monumental task of either convincing him to continue or stepping in to fix things yourself.

Overall, a deeply atmospheric and morally complex adventure with very interesting puzzle solutions.

review:
On the positive side this game is a modern update to classics like NBA Hangtime & NBA Jam Tournament Edition. 

However, a few key areas of game play make this quite frustrating to have a "flow" to the game.

Suggestions below can be improved upon and hopefully made better in the next patches.

1) Rebounding. The rebounding/box out is seemingly random or heavily favored to the AI for offensive rebounds. At least 5 times to ten times a game in three minutes both my player and CPU player are standing over a basketball on the ground and cannot pick it up while the AI opponent casually walks over and grabs the ball. This is very frustrating over 3 minutes of play.

2) Cross-over dribbling. While excellent, they wipe out 1/2 or more stamina even on players with a high stamina rating. This would never happen in most arcade games so I hope this can be adjusted to allow for multiple cross overs or an option for unlimited.

3) Fade away jumpers. The difficulty in converting a fade away jump shot is almost impossible. I have played as "legend" Tracy McGrady and his shot bar for success on a fade away jump shot is so small and such a difficult narrow window to press shoot that is becomes almost useless to attempt a fade away.

4) Online play. I agree experience points are useful before online play. However, my first opponent played with a team containing Paul George and blocked my shot 10 times and scored at least five three pointers and was next to unguardable. Even Alonzo Mourning could not block dunks in the paint.

5) Clear outs / steal attempts. Same frustrating challenge as cross-over dribbling. One steal attempt or push attempt should not clear out over 33% of stamina. I understand this is not an unlimited turbo game with unlimited pushing and am not asking for that. I think three push attempts per 100% stamina is not too much to ask here is it? There seems to be overcompensation for foulless games and like the game NBA Showtime: NBA ON NBC on Nintendo 64.  At least consider an "arcade" mode and simulation mode if that is the key. I thought this game was more "arcade" but it seems to hold onto a bit too much "simulation" in games.

Considering I have 3 hours of gameplay it very well could be that I need to play another 15-20 hours to get my experience points up to increase stamina but it seems unlikely.

Graphics are pretty nice (GTX 970, 16GB RAM, I7 3.4 GHZ Intel Processor, 1TB HDD). 

The player cards are fun and I like the random aspect of obtaining "average" to "legend" players in the player packs.

review:
I've enjoyed a good amount of this game considering I wouldn't have put in the hours I did unless I had some degree of enjoyment. However, even with 2 updates there are still some issues

1) FIX THE NETCODE: The first online match I had was laggy so much that I was dunked on when I had the ball. Then Whenever I was going to shoot a 3 pointer, I had the ball stolen from me out of nowhere. 

2) Repeat cards on maxed out players: If I take the time to grind out a player that has terrible stats, I don't want to see them come into a player pack because the exp they get is WORTHLESS. There are mobile games that understand duplicates on maxed out characters shouldn't exist and those are free to play.

3) The lottery tickets punish people for winning too much: If I am winning by 9 points, this gives the enemy team something like double points or the mystery stars and on higher difficulty AI, they couldn't be anywhere near it and still win. This disincentivizes me from playing how I want to play and if I am 7 points ahead, then I just am throwing the ball around before they inevitably get a 3 pointer perfect shot. Making it to where that 7 point lead is now a 3 point lead all because I don't want them scoring 20 points from some bogus scoring mechanic. There needs to be a cutoff on it to where it's not becoming a deliberate losing is winning like Mario Kart.

4) Perfect shots make zero sense without any given context: I don't know if it's asking for me to hit the very beginning, center, or the very end. If the game would clarify, that'd be great.

5) The tutorial doesn't cover enough: I don't know when I should be pressing the steal button or when they are open to be stolen from and it results in braindead mashing of it. There isn't anything on blocking shots or when those windows are covered leading me to either shove or steal instead because those don't have as large of recovery.

6) The AI became unforgiving around level 29. I will set the difficulty on easy and have the enemy AI with characters that have 3s and 4s for blocks come out to be able to block every single dunk am

7) Shuffling has no counters: I've had so many AI matches where they just spammed the passing and shuffling towards the basket and that's how they score. Blocking has already been shown as ineffective without any showing as to why it didn't work. The passing spam can't be blocked by the steal button or the y button. Then, shoving becomes useless because they receive it and shuffle, now I have no stamina, they can sprint and dunk and fill lottery meter. 

8) Speaking of shoving: Shoving has more times than not only delayed them from scoring. I would shove them and the same player I shoved got the ball back. This means the shove button has more recovery than the person being shoved in a lot of cases. Then what was the point in shoving them?

9) WHY DOES AN OFFLINE MODE LIKE EXHIBITION REQUIRE AN INTERNET CONNECTION? I had a few internet outages yesterday and not being able to play offline is a glaring issue that I don't understand. If they are that concerned with people cheating the card packs then require an internet connection to open them. If you don't want them scumming the exp, then why not turn off exp in offline if they are that concerned? 

10) Online mode is only against randos: It's 2017, people played NBA Jam with their friends back in 1993 locally and in 2010 there was a game in which you could play with friends online in 2010. This is a game people want to play with friends and some friends are half the country away. Get with the picture.

11) Character Balancing: It isn't a fair game when someone is using 2 legendaries against 2 commons. This is just screaming for people to meta-whore and all you are going to see are the 2 same players over and over again. Have a character level limit which forbids legendaries from going against commons, epics against commons, or legendaries against commons.

All of that being said this game is good. It's a good game to pick up and play for 30 minutes, but after that, it can become repetitive.

review:
I bought this game looking for something to play for 2 hours and then be done with it, but little did I expect to get a full day worth of enjoyment. NBA Playgrounds is a switch on those classic NBA Jam & NBA Street games. It is much more fast paced and fluent than those past games. You Start the game with a handful of "Player Packs" in order to get your dynamic duo of a team started. I really enjoy the Pack System in this game because it gave me some incentive to want to level up. I have played past NBA 2K games (2K10-2K17) and I feel as though that [b] 2K can learn something from Saber Interactive. [/b] The soundtrack and art style of this game is phenomenal and it only add's to the games zaniness and laid back attitude. NBA Playgrounds doesn't take itself too seriously, which is something I am in love with. Allen Iverson teaming throwing a 20-foot high alley-oop to Demar Derozan while dabbing is something I can highly appreciate and watch all day. There are over 150+ players for you to collect through player packs with NO MICROTRANSACTIONS, yes that means that you will have to actually play the game and gain some knowledge and skill in order to get some of the best players (Take a hint 2K). Some issues I have with the game are the Lottery Pick system and the game's content going forward. I feel as though the Lottery Pick system is a bit too RNG based for this game, I feel as though maybe if it wasn't earned as easy it would be more balanced. As for the long term, I hope they do not mess up the system of which they have already. I do hope they release more packs and tournaments throughout the updates but please DO NOT MAKE THEM BUYABLE. One of my favorite things about this game is how satisfying it is to unlock your favorite character after an hour or so of leveling and I feel as though putting in any sort of microtransactions would solely kill that feeling altogether. All together NBA Playgrounds is a fantastic game with some very minor tweaks. NBA fan or not, this is a definite pickup for anybody looking for some crazy fun. 

====================================================================================

**EDIT AFTER WRITING**
I totally forgot about the online portion of this game when writing my initial review, so let me address that here. The online portion is very fun... when it decides to work. I love seeing all of the combinations of players other players put together and it makes for some very interesting games. However most of the time I find myself lagging majorly or losing connection midway through a game. It seems as though multiple people are currently having this problem, so as the game is updated more you can most likely expect this problem to be fixed. 

====================================================================================

PROS:
-Very fast and fluent gameplay 
-Art Style and Soundtrack are very fitting 
-Loads of replay ability 
-Tournament Mode
-Pack System
-No Microtransactions 
-In-depth Player Information

====================================================================================

CONS:
-Lottery Pick System
-Online Servers 
-Longterm?

review:
[i] IN-DEPTH REVIEW. As someone who grew up playing thousands of hours of NBA JAM and NBA JAM Tournament Edition, I want to write this review for those familiar with NBA JAM (simplified sports games) and those not familiar with these games. I'll try to explain both [/i]

_____________________

This game in my mind is a cross between NBA Jam and Freestyle Basketball 2. 

It is a 2v2 basketball game that is highly dependent on a) Timing b) momentum management c) character matchups. 

This game is similar to NBA Jam (hereafter referred to as NBAJ) in that it is a 2v2 basketball game with sprint/boost, shoves, elbow throws, super flying dunks, power ups. Its dunks, blocks, steals, shooting and defense are all VERY TIMING based. Just like NBAJ. But the timing is even more strict and takes awhile to learn, unlike NBAJ.

It also has important character stats like shooting, dunking, 2 pointers, 3 pointers, steals, blocks, stamina, speed, rebounding. Keep in mind 2 pointers and dunks are different things. Basically each of these have their own timing window and better ratings allow you more forgiving timing window.

This game is different from NBAJ in that [b] momentum management [/b] is hugely important. This is similar to Freestyle basketball 2. Basically, the way you open the defense up is by getting them to jump on your pump fake or be too aggressive on defense. Doing so will pigeonhole the defender into a certain type of defense, which u can exploit.

As an example, if you receive a pass, you pump fake and the defender jumps super high to block. You then move slightly over and shoot a free 3 pointer. Or you receive the pass and defender tries to steal, in which case you throw elbows and knock him back. It's basically a counter-counter mind game.

NBAJ had some of this but you could recover on defense much faster because there wasn't really momentum applied to the characters besides jumping. Here, even a bad steal attempt and especially a bad shove attempt puts you out of position on defense.

Other features to consider:

Stamina - 

So there was a turbo meter in NBAJ but in this game you need to learn to defend well without relying on steal/shove. You need to learn timings and positioning. A shove attempt completely depletes your stamina and it's hard to land. A steal attempt takes less stamina but about 3 attempts completely depletes you. This is even if you never sprint on defense, which you will. 

This is because the offense has a juke move on Right stick, another major difference from NBAJ. I actually like this change because people and PGs who are great at steals can MURDER you in NBAJ and games like this. Juking does take about half your stamina though, but it gives u a slight boost downcourt as well. Dunking also takes a lot of stamina and if you don't have any you will do a layup instead.

Timing -

Dunking and shooting timings are very strict and hard to learn at first. If you miss, it will tell you "early" or "late". It's tough but you will learn it eventually. It may be offputting to younger gamers, but this type of "just play until you learn it" mechanic is totally normal if you grew up playing Super NES or Sega genesis. 

Defense -

As I mentioned before it's hard. You may feel just go offense and outscore your opponent. But if you DO have a solid defense, you can just destroy your opponent. The game is very snowball due to power ups I mention below.

You cannot goal tend like you could in NBAJ. Well, in NBAJ you could basically catch the ball out of the air by lining up with it on its way up (and slightly on its way down even). In this game you need to play close defense and time your jump to block their shots. Great blockers will jump SUPER high to block a jump shot. 

For blocking dunks it's more about jumping WITH the dunker and matching his momentum. If you do, you will basically collide in the air with him and knock out the ball

On Fire system -

There is no on fire system like NBAJ. But there is a power up system. If you fill a certain power bar, you get a random mario kart like powerup (infinite stamina, guaranteed 3 pointer, etc). To fill the bar you must perform well, and if your opponent dunks on your face it can lower your bar.

So, this is very much a rich-get-richer type of system. Not sure how I feel about that, I feel they should be exclusive of each other OR actually help the loser catchup. 

Characters -

Thank god there's no micro$ in this game to get characters. But you will have to play and "level up" to get player packs and unlock players. I'm guessing that you eventually get every player in game just by playing. That is good. 

You need to find your playstyle and what characters you want to use. Right now, it's pretty much all Shaq and Curry. But player matchups are definitely a thing.

_____

[b] Needs fixing [/b]

- Audio bug. Cannot save music level and it's loud

- If you receive a pass and throw elbows, you cannot dribble after, which is wrong basketball-wise. You can catch and pump fake then dribble, which is correct. But an arm movement doesn't preclude you from starting a dribble. This should be fixed.

- multiplayer. I personally can't find any match. I've changed my Steam Download region to Asia, US-Los Angeles, New York and London. Found one match. So I'm guessing mp is broken pretty much. I just queued for 25 min on US-LA region while writing this review. 

Also keep in mind [b] There is no 2v2 right now. And there is no friend invites. The only mp is playing random 1v1 online. If you want this to play with friends, I recommend to WAIT and DO NOT BUY [/b]

- FPS lock. It's locked to 60 fps. Would be nice to have 144 fps but I'm guessing this won't happen

[h] Conclusion [/h]

I do recommend this given you understand all the above and like these mechanics. However, if you want a more relaxing or forgiving sports game, it may not be for you.

I also forsee a "meta" unfortunately forming based on certain things (namely dunking into alley oop pass and dunk) being incredibly efficient in terms of success rate. There needs to be dunking teams, 2 pointer teams, 3 pointer teams, and defensive / rebounding teams viable. 

But I do now know if the devs have the means or will to make this competitively balanced. This is a 20$ game after all. We will see.

Feel free to comment on this review if you have questions. I'm very passionate about sports games like this and Super Mega Baseball and Rocket League .

review:
This is a solid NBA Jam-style game, but it needs an update to go from a mediocre game to a good one.

[b]Positives:[/b]
[list]
    [*]It's gorgeous. The player caricatures are hilarious.
    [*]Its overall gameplay is decent. At the time of writing this review, it is a fun arcade game.
    [*]While the game requires you to unlock all players, you can do this through playing the game instead of having to buy random packs. There are no players that are extremely rare or expensive to get and a reasonable fee unlocks them all if that is what you want.
    [*]Upgrading players goes fast and unlocks cosmetic changes. The stats stay the same.
[/list]

[b]Negatives:[/b]
[list]
    [*]The person who did the stats for the players made some ridiculous decisions. Tracy McGrady, Dr. J, Zack LaVine, Gerald Green, Shawn Kemp might be some of the best dunkers of all time but in this game none of them are 10s. Ben Wallace is an average rebounder, and Roy Hibbert is a better shot blocker than Wilt Chamberlain. Celtics' Shaq is one of the best 2PT scorers in the game, Ricky Rubio is a 10 for steals, Roy Hibbert is one of the best defensive big men, Tony Parker is a 9 on threes, and the Celtics' Ray Allen is a better dunker than the Bucks' Ray Allen. Kevin Durant is an average shooter and LeBron is just a dunker; don't expect him to be good at defense or rebounding. Why they could not just make the great players great is beyond me. You don't play this kind a game to have your favorite player be a scrub (or simply play like someone else). Just hand out more 10s and make some players (like Wilt and LeBron) truly dominant across the board.
    [*]Nobody seems to be playing this online at the time. It is still very fun to play with your friends in coop.
The game's stamina feature could use an update. Instead of not letting me do a defensive move when I am out of stamina, it would be better if the effectiveness would just go down.
    [*]The dribble moves have no real function, at least not against the CPU.
[/list]

[b]Neutral:[/b]
[list]
    [*]3PT shooting is overpowered. You can defeat the computer with Ray Allen or Dirk Nowitzki by shooting threes and not running back on defense. I won a tournament finals game 45-20 by doing that. I don't think that the 3PT shooting effectiveness should be taken down though. However, this issue goes away when playing real players so I do not feel that this should be changed.
    [*]Some other reviews complain about RNG. Sports games often have RNG as it feels more realistic. There is a very small percentage chance that a perfect shot will go out, and honestly, that is fine with me. You can shoot a basketball with perfect mechanics and still miss.
[/list]

review:
I want to like this game.  I really, really want to like this game.

When I initially started playing, I was having a lot of fun playing against the CPU.  Learning how to play the game, trying to figure out the timing of shots, and playing through the tournaments.  However, I knew that this fun would not last forever, as the real crux of these kind of games is the multiplayer.  So I finally jumped on to play some online games and what do I get?  Probably one of the most frustrating experiences I've ever had playing a basketball game.

I played multiple matches, and it all boiled down to this:  The opposing team would send their Steph Curry to the opposite side of the cart, wait for the clock to run down, and shoot from 90 feet away.  They'd make it about 25% of the time, which is already a big giant red flag for me.  

Okay, you'll say, but if that's all he's shooting you can easily outscore them.  That would work, except that rebounding is inherently broken.  If you don't control the rebounder, your teammate's AI decides to run out to the three point line to contest the shot, then realize they can't and run back under the basket which is always later than the opposing player's AI.  If you ARE controlling the rebounder, you can expect the AI to never play defense on the other side of the court, and grabbing a rebound is incredibly frustrating.  It's impossible to jump and grab a rebound, because your player will just go flying into the air towards god knows where.  You have to walk towards where the ball is going to be which, again, wouldn't be an issue if the opposing player's AI didn't somehow magically know where the ball was going to bounce and get to it before you.

Even with Dwight Howard, I'd be standing directly underneath where the ball was going to land and the opposing team's Steph Curry would casually walk over and go into what I call the rebounding animation of stupidity.  The game decides who's going to get the ball before the ball is grabbed. That player will then look upwards and very, very slowly walk towards the ball.  It doesn't matter if somebody else gets to the position before that player since that player has already been prematurely chosen as the rebounder.

Then there's the shooting.  I had to go online and do research on what the shot timing is supposed to be.  I've played basketball games all my life from NBA Jam to 2k17, and I've never had an issue with shot release timing.  In this game, it seems the shot release has nothing to do with your actual player's animation.  It's much easier to stand in the corner and shoot a three than it is to try and time a layup in this game, which is ridiculous.

Then there's the powerups.  A fun but gamebreaking (see what I did there) addition to the NBA Street games, in Playgrounds the powerups are not created equal and can therefore single handedly win a team a game.  Oh look, I got the powerup that allows me to score a shot with 100% accuracy.  The opponent gets the powerup that doubles their dunk points... and it lasts multiple possessions.  Takes a lot of the skill out of the game.

Finally there's the stealing.  It happens in about 50% of the games.  The opposing team will be about five feet away from me, mash the steal button, and knock the ball away 100% of the time.  I mean it.  Literally 100% of the time steal mashing would work for those players.

Again, I would absolutely love to be able to enjoy this game, but with online broken like it is I just can't see myself playing it again any time soon.  Because of that, I'll be asking for a refund.

tl;dr:  Fun concept, but the online is broken in incredibly frustrating ways.  Would not recommend.

review:
I'm 3hrs into the game so far. There are a lot of pros and cons to it. I got it for $1.99, and at that price it's an absolute steal. It takes me back to my days of NBA Jam, but with a bit more depth. I actually like the card pack system as it makes you play different players, rather than just being a fan who plays the same 2 guys the entire duration of their time in the game.

I think the controls are fairly bad for how nice the game looks. There are times where Im extremely frustrated with getting rebounds. As a casual player who only plans to play th PvE side of the game, and not dedicate hours to it, your AI teammates just standing there not trying to help grab a rebound is really annoying. Especially when Im really trying hard to do the challenge, and the opposing team ends up with possession for nearly a minute straight. This has actually happened a number of times. There have been a few challenges so far that need the full game time running at a pretty fast pace (20pts with just 2pt jump shots comes to mind). For someone not trying to put in a lot of time to get amazing at the game to play ranked, this part feels super clunky.

I think player movement could be a bit smoother, too. It also feels a bit clunky. It's not awful, but def noticeable. 

I do wish there was some form of reroll system for cards. Any double automatically get burned and turned into xp for their player. I wish they would let you collect doubles and either cash them in for xp, or choose X to reroll into a random card. In League of Legends (My main time sink), you can do this with skin shards. If you dont like the skin shards you've got from boxes and dont want to craft them, you can reroll 3 into a random skin. The only way to get packs right now is to gain levels and do all challenges in a tournament for a Legendary pack. At least as far as I know.

I know NP2 is coming out later this month. I hope some of these things have been worked on. Id also like to see some form of player creator with a story mode. No idea if they're looking into that, but it would add a lot of depth to the game.

But overall Im really enjoying the game. Great NBA Jam nostalgia. Easily worth it on sale. 

Now just give me my Dominique Wilkins already!

review:
I was hoping for a nice updated version of NBA Hangtime. What I got was a frustrating mix of things on top of some good ideas.

The card/pack system to unlock players is a good idea. However, it takes WAY too long to earn enough XP to get just one pack, which is just random players (and I'm guessing other things like different parks, which makes it even worse). XP per level has fluctuated, and I don't understand why.

Leveling specific players is also cool, but again, it takes way too long. Especially considering how many players there are. Plus, from what I can tell, the only thing you get for leveling is new moves, which don't actually improve anything.

Gameplay:

The shot meter is a terrible idea, as it forces you to look away from the action. Not only that, it's really bothersome to have layups and dunks constantly missing, even when uncontested. Even with the meter in the green, they miss. Those are 99% accuracy shots, but my percentage is way below that. It's impossible to make shots with any kind of consistency. Turn off the shot meter and you literally can't make anything. Older games just suggested you release the shot at the height of your jump, and used that plus the players own stats to determine how accurate the shot is. Forcing us to look away from high-action is not a good idea.

The A.I. in this game is absurd. Even on rookie difficulty, it's hard as balls. The opponents block every shot, knock you out on every dunk, contest everything.

Inputs don't work. Telling your teammate to go up for an alley-oop works very rarely. Pushing is bugged, it works when it wants to.

Even though the opponent A.I. is so smart, your teammate is dumb as a rock and will mostly just stand there. You can't have it both ways.

The shot clock is random. I don't know if it's a feature or bug that the time on the shot clock doesn't always reset, but it's absolutely stupid either way. Also add to this getting more points for doing certain things, that aren't well explained.

Stealing is pointless. Nine times out of ten, if you swipe the ball out of their hands, it will end up right back in their hands. Same with pushing them, forcing the ball out.

I can't recommend this game as is, but it has potential to be a great successor to NBA Jam/Hangtime.

review:
I love walking sims. I love games that touch on tricky topics. This game does both, and it also has moments of beauty and sadness. In theory, I should love Anamorphine.

Unfortuntely, the current version has too many issues to recommend it. These issues include bad event triggers, unclear ways forward, repeated content, and disorientation.

With the bad event triggers, sometimes you'll even be standing or looking in the right place but the next scene just won't start, so you end up backtracking unnecessarily. This can mean wasting minutes, losing the flow of the game, and generally becoming unnecessarily frustrated.

The unclear pathing is also quite a problem. While the game is set up to have *some* of this on purpose, so that you as a player feel some of the same disorientation as your character, overall it feels less thought out. You end up backtracking when you don't need to. At times, you can't tell which way to go to progress the story, only to find out that there's a path that looks just like the one you were already on but instead moves you along in the story.

One of the nice things about walking sims is that you can get treated to some cool "mini game" style areas where you explore different aspects of the world (like the different character stories in What Remains of Edith Finch). Unfortuntely, in Anamorphine, the developers have chosen to reuse problematic game elements, forcing you to replay "mini game" style areas over and over. Even though they provided some differences, the overall effect feels like one of repetition and tedium without any "aha!" or breakthrough moment.

Sadly, the last of the four caused me to stop the game: disorientation which caused motion-sickness. I would have liked to finish it, but simply wasn't able to get past the area without feeling nauseous.  I think this could have been fixed with better play-testing and pathing.

With luck, future versions will address these issues and help Anamorphine live up to its promise.

Anamorphine breaks new ground in so many ways that it's hard not to recommend it to anyone who likes alternative and experimental games. 

You progress through the story fluidly without any loading, cut or jump: instead, there are seamless transition across time and space that put you in a dreamlike feeling of not knowing how you got to where you are, nor how to leave. It is beautiful and anxiogenic at once, and it reminds me of the Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind in that regard -- that's definitely a compliment. 

Overall, the surrealist imagery does a surprisingly good job of walking you through the somber themes of addiction, loss and escapism. For a narrative built on that subtlety and nuance, it's a feat of storytelling to entirely avoid words and still get the emotion across.

I only wish there had been more time and scenes to dig deeper into Elena and Tyler's psyches. Even though I understood their distress, I came just a bit shy of truly identifying and empathizing with them, except for one or two brief but truly touching moments. Regardless, Anamorphine is a giant leap forward in conveying meaning and emotion through mechanics, and I hope we'll see more of those mind-bending adventures from Artifact 5 in the future.

review:
May be mild spoilers ahead:

As someone who generally loves slow, artsy walking simulators, I am astonished at how incredibly bad this game is.  It is so bad that I am literally suspicious of all of the positive reviews on this.  The game is cumbersome, buggy, controls awkwardly, reuses the same handful of ugly environments ad nauseum...  the level design is bland, confusing, and has no sense of direction... the visual aesthetic is almost aggressively bland, and the sole animated character is lifeless and unexpressive (even when surrounded by literal statues)... the story is almost comically melodramatic, and did not earn its shocking, morbid ending... the camera occasionally turns into a bouncing, juddering mess... 

There is a scene early on where you ride a bicycle.  It controls awkwardly, and while you are basically forced to follow a bland, linear path for several minutes, the level geometry will fail miserably if you veer even slightly off path.  I remember hoping that this was an unfortunate road bump, and that the rest of the game won't be this bad.  The game then goes on to use the bicycle mechanic around five times, through increasingly bland and repetitive landscapes, which eventually lose any sense of flow and leave you wondering where to go, but will still punish you with janky camera and failing geometry if you veer off path.

There was a moment where a character was in a bath, and the water didn't load properly, instead displaying the wrong image file where the water should be.  There were several unbearable minutes where I was forced to walk around a spiral staircase while my movement speed (even my look speed!) were reduced to maybe one tenth of normal speed, for no discernible reason.  I got stuck behind invisible walls that suddenly became passable seconds later.  The game also repeats scenes a lot.  I think without repetition or unnecessary slow downs and padding, the game would be over in 20 mins.  

Sorry if this sounds harsh, and if this is in any way based on someone's person experience, I can understand that maybe they were using development to work through some things.  I've actually lived through some very similar experiences to what is shown in this game, and I can understand struggling to express some of the very complicated emotions that go with this territory.  That said, this is a piece of art released to the public, and demanding of criticism.  This is a commercial product, not a private diary.  As a game, this does very few things, and none of them well.  The best thing I can say about the game is that the scene transitions are occasionally interesting when they work properly.

review:
First of all, credit to the devs for continuing to update the game and fix issues as they pop up. While some of the problems early on should absolutely have been addressed before launch (good controller support, in particular), I appreciate that they're trying to polish the product as they receive feedback. When an update broke the intro for a particular boss, I was able to reach out on the devs' discord and they pushed out a new update within an hour.

Make no mistake: this is HEAVILY inspired by Cave Story. The graphics, music, platforming, gun styles, and level themes range from "reminiscent" to "nearly a direct copy," and this ends up being both good and bad. In some ways, "More Cave Story" is a good time, but at other times you can't help but think about how the original is better.

As a metrodvania, the gameplay is solid, with plenty of secrets and collectables to seek out. The movement options that get introduced later in the game are legitimately fun and help keep things face-paced. Optional upgrades for your guns help keep things fresh, but by the end of the game I found that most of my weapons had fallen by the wayside in favor of just a couple high-damage options.

The boss design is hit-and-miss, and mainly suffers from being bland and one-note. Even in some of the later fights with (probably too many) phases, each phase is just about cycling through 1-3 attacks that you can just develop a rote pattern for. The designers try to add some variety by changing the boss arenas through each phase, but mostly that just serves to mask the simplicity of the boss attacks.

The weakest part of the game for me was probably the "digital" world where you play as the Avatar Duo. It felt simultaneously unnecessary and under-utilized. The platforming all feels the same, the "double" character doesn't add anything meaningful to the gameplay, the bosses are even more straightforward than the standard ones, and the last powerup you earn for the duo is barely relevant. It feels tacked on in a way, and it's used inconsistently. At first, you get the impression that one of the main reasons you play as the Duo is to unlock powerups for the main character, like when you gain the ability to pick up heavy objects...but later, your most important upgrades just happen automatically. They even say something to the effect of "We fixed this while you were doing other stuff!" Why didn't we play through an area to unlock that ability like before?

review:
I feel guilty for only paying 99 cents for this. It's definitely worth more.

I'm about 2.5 hours into the puzzles and I'm only 57% done with the first section of three. There's a lot more ground to cover.

RYB is an extremely abstract puzzle game. You are presented with an arrangement of black tiles on a white screen. Some of the tiles have colored dots inside them. The dots indicate the colors of adjacent tiles, and successfully picking the color of a tile may or may not reveal more dots on it. It sounds really simple, but there is a brain-burn the deeper into the puzzles you go.

You start out simple, with only red and yellow dots, then blue is added a little later. (Hence the name of the game, RYB.) It doesn't stop there, as orange, green, and purple eventually get mixed into play. The puzzling portion really kicks in as you realize that, just like we learned in kindergarten, red plus yellow makes orange. If orange is in a puzzle, then it's entirely possible that a red dot in one tile means there's an orange tile next to it. Soon you're thinking a tile is "yellowish", because it has to be yellow, orange, or green (yellow plus blue), but it can't be purple because that's only red plus blue. review: It is with great displeasure that I give this game a negative review. I'm a fan of FLEB's YouTube channel, so I went into RYB with high expectations that were not met. I played through the entire game, 100%, and at no point did I feel like there was some grand "eureka" moment where I'd discovered some nuance the puzzle was trying to coax me into finding. The entire time I felt like I was going off of strong hunches that were almost always correct. Good puzzle design will often lure the solver into a trap to force them to think critically about some false assumption or something, but most of the puzzles just lured me straight into the solution. The few puzzles that I didn't solve straight away were usually the result of tunnel vision more than anything. Maybe this is a game targeted towards those newer to puzzle games and I've just been spoiled by tougher games in the genre. In that case, I still wouldn't recommend the game, because it doesn't feel great to play, either. I'm willing to forgive the strange default keyboard layout, since I think that can be changed in the settings, but I'm not willing to forgive the graphics. I understand that not every puzzle designer is also a graphic designer, but I don't think it would've been terribly difficult for FLEB to show his game to a few people and ask if it looks okay before publishing. The yellow is really, really bright, especially against the white background, and I think a thin, black outline could've gone a long way towards remedying this. It's also a real shame that this game is based purely on color, leaving out colorblind players who might've enjoyed playing this. Modern design practices usually involve the use of symbols corresponding to each color to accommodate, although I've not sure how that would work with the secondary color mechanic. I also think a Sudoku-style note system could've gone a long way towards making the later puzzles feel like a thing that could be intuitively worked out, and at that point it would've made sense to include some tougher puzzles that would require the use of such notes.

review:
I am 32 years old.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.

Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.

With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.

After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.

Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.

Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.

Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you.

review:
This game is an action game with a narrator that tries to be like the one from the Stanley Parable. Except he isn't quite as good or interesting on the delivery and sounds like he's just complaining a lot of the time... Most, if not all, of the game, you are making decisions by your actions based upon whether you want to follow the narrator or not. Each of the off-path choices tends to unlock a different "end" and shows some lore about the story. 

The action parts are ok. There are a lot of skills you can get and upgrade. The game doesn't use a skill tree system, and you can upgrade whatever skill you want to, if you have the money. However, it is well beyond me to see how you can earn enough money to upgrade even more than a handful of skills to max, even in a 100% achievements playthrough (which I did), unless you farm like crazy (which I won't do). I ended up just increasing her base stats and base combo - I guess it was enough, but I feel like I missed out on a lot of the interesting fight potential of the game. The fighting wasn't so exciting that I feel like I'd go back to upgrade all the skills, though.

The story.. well there are different layers to it. Maybe I just didn't quite get it. The narrator, himself, is a bit confusing as he seems to play different roles in the story at times (though he is always trying to guide you/ICEY/UCEY?). I won't spoil anything, but I feel like the makers of the game were trying different ideas, but couldn't decide which one to stick with.

Honestly, I can't recommend this game at full price ($10.99). Maybe get it when it's on sale, and only if you enjoy Stanley Parable-like narrator style. (I did enjoy that style, so it's ok by me). For other people looking for a pure action game, it might be better to play something else.

review:
Recommended on sale, probably not at full price, if you are picking this game up in 2025 and beyond.  I think there are other indie 2D action games with better value for the bucks.

An enjoyable, if short, side-scrolling action game with a fairly enjoyable combat experience.  I will say it is not a particularly well-designed one though, despite the flashy, DMC Vergil-like stylish katana girl video you may come across online.  While ICEY's moveset is cool and feels good to practice/execute, the interaction with enemies (both mobs and bosses) isn't particularly well-thought out.  Throwing around never-stopping hyperarmored mobs is [i]not[/i] a fun experience, especially when your avatar's damage animation does not seem to have i-frames, leading to frequent stunlocks.  It's still an overall fun combat flow (trying to clear that secret room without using the "cheat" felt good), but it's a missed opportunity when experimenting with majority of the moveset simply increases your risk with very little reward.

I will say the combat being very lenient with animation cancelling was nice though.  I could chain a launcher + helmbreaker so quickly that it's like I was standing on the spot, chopping up and down with very high flexibility.  Reminded me of some techs from X4 Zero after all this time.

The "story" is...enjoyable, I guess?  I played in Japanese, and the Narrator's VA was pretty good, so maybe that helped too.  But it's definitely "not for everyone," and in my view not in a good way.  It's something you [i]may[/i] enjoy if you're sort of in on the joke kind of deal.  Let's just say phrases like "not for everyone" mentioned above, or "play it without spoiling yourself" usually invokes an expectation of some serious, dramatic story experience but...temper your expectation, this game ain't it.

Overall, a nice cheap, short action game to pick up for a chill fun.

The latter is particularly annoying because you then have to remake the burger from scratch because the game has touchy hitboxes or something.

review:
I actually really enjoyed this.

Eltariel is only grating if you don't understand where she's coming from. Talion is being corrupted by the Nazgul's ring, just like all the other kings and queens that fell, and Eltariel is trying to help him regardless because she sees the good he can still do. Her "betraying" him at the end of the DLC was inevitable, just like his corruption into a Nazgul. She literally said she strikes down men corrupted by the Rings. She knows how seductive that power is and how it corrupts. If anyone thought Talion could resist forever, they're a fool.

(Additionally, her taking the Ring at the climax of the base game is deeply understandable? The kings of Men failed the Elves when Isildur refused to destroy the One Ring. She has every reason to take that power for Galadriel instead; Men have proven themselves untrustworthy in the past. For fuck's sake, Talion gave the Ring to *Shelob*.)

The Nazgul Sisters were cool as hell and show just how far Sauron's tendrils crept in the world of Man. People bashing them for being "DEI" are just angry they saw women in a video game because they don't perceive women as anything but a pair of ovaries, much less a person. Their boss fight is actually pretty fun, imo--especially if you have the all-around light instead of the focused one.

The Light mechanic is so much fun and my only complaint is how many Captains are immune to it. You don't really have many options for dealing with Uruk-hai compared to Talion; it's kind of just the Light and your blades. That being said, the Light being so much fun totally makes up for it; blinding Orcs and using that to attack them? It takes you feel like a veritable Elven ninja, which is only expanded on when you get the Light Bringer's Dagger and get to go invisible every time you brutalize an enemy. It creates an awesome feedback loop of "blind opponent, stab them, go invisible and stab more". I say again: Elven ninja. (This also makes the Light Bringer Dagger a rather funny metatextual commentary; you are encouraged to be *more* brutal in your kills, which is befitting of Elvish hatred for the Orcs. Remember how Sting glows when Orcs are near because it was made by Elven smiths that despised Orcs?)

The story is short, but has its moments. I won't say its high art but the fights against the Nazgul Sisters and Talion are fun and the infiltration of a Fortress to assassinate the Overlord was something I really, really enjoyed. As much fun as assaulting a fortress is, sometimes I want to slit throats and call it a day, you know? And for those of you who are fans of fortress assaults--don't worry, you get to both defend and attack a fortress.

In conclusion: I give it an A- and say it's worth your money.

review:
This game was a great surprise! Not sure why I had it on my priority backlog, but I had tons of fun!

Ghostory is a puzzle-platformer game (more puzzle than platformer) with retro graphics that will challenge your brain.

The premise is simple, but really well explored: You can turn between normal and ghost forms, but you also need to carry your backpack with you, and you can only carry it while being corporeal. While in ghost form, you can fly around and through stuff, and you need to constantly switch between forms in order to bring your backpack through the levels.

A few highlights:
- Smooth difficulty progression. First levels are small and easy, with few different elements. Later on, the levels become huge, with multiple new elements being added as your progress through the story.
- Very smart puzzles. You can see a lot of effort's been put into the puzzles. It may take a while to figure out what you need to do, but once you do it's very rewarding. Be ready to spend an hour or more on later levels (there are 28 of them, plus interludes)!
- Little focus on platforming. Not sure about you, but when I play puzzle-platformers, I'm not a fan of games that put a lot of emphasis on the precision platforming aspect, and require you to do tons of precise jumping very fast. Some of the platforming sections are a bit harder, sure, but they all seem fair (if they don't, you're probably trying to do the wrong thing).
- Extra side quests. Besides going through the levels, there are also some side missions that you can complete for an extra challenge. This included collecting artifacts with your backpack, herding frogs into their homes and other stuff.

If you're into this kind of game, be sure to give it a try, this is probably one of my favorite indie games in the genre, and on top of that it's cheap!

You pick a story. Read through a series of comicbook-styled stills, watch a sex scene, and then read some more.

[h1]Story[/h1]
As this game is a series of short stories, I'll provide a synopsis for each one that is currently available; In "A New Companion", Michael orders a non-so-virtual [i]ass[/i]istant; In "Foreman's Foreplay", a ladyfriend rewards Michael for helping her beat a level in her game; In "Streaming Secrets", Michael stumbles upon a sexually charged dynamic duo; In "Forbidden Pleasure", Michael's living quarters loses power, and he winds up in the bar in search of a [i]quickie[/i]; finally, in "Punishment Served", Michael finds himself under arrest, but his officer is bored and horny.

The game boots into the "Choose a Story" screen, where you can pick a (previously unlocked) tale to read. The interface looks darned good — it's [i]very[/i] aesthetically pleasing, and meshes well with the overall sci-fi theme. From "Settings", you can adjust graphical and resolution preferences. It's unclear how the "Graphics Quality" slider affects the in-game visuals, and I would have liked to have been able to adjust individual graphical settings (such as anti-aliasing or depth of field). Oh and there's a ton of clipping!

I had mixed feelings about the goodies. The models look alright, but they often appear fuzzy or lifeless. The sex scenes sport a solid roster of positions to put each actor in. I hate to say it, but [i]wait for a sale.[/i] I really like the idea behind this game — a collection of one-off stories followed with senseless bangin'? You can count me in. But given the playtime and rough edges, I would suggest waiting for a light sale, or a few solid updates.

review:
Gorgeous game in looks and gameplay.

Faeria also combines card collection, deck building and tactical combat played out on a map. The unique feature is that as part of each match players also *build* the map. This transforms the choices presented for deck archetypes such as control, aggro and rush.

For context, I have played and enjoyed Poxnora, Hearthstone and Duelyst in that order. Of these, Poxnora *was* my easy favourite thanks to combining card collection and deck building with very deep tactical combat played out on a variety of maps. I can no longer cope with the complexity of Poxnora.

In contrast to Poxnora the game is simpler to learn and quicker to play. In contrast to Duelyst and Hearthstone my early experience is that trick decks and unbeatable combinations are less likely making the tactical combat choices matter far more. If you are familiar with Hearthstone and Duelyst you will find present similar modes of play including - 

# Solo play of battles and puzzles
# Constructed deck play
# Tournament play, using a deck constructed from a series of choices offered

***Big Positives***

# Beautiful, relaxing visuals and matching music
# Deck "formulas" are built into the game offering an easy start for new players
# Developer offers a hub for played designed decks, also helpful for new players
# Significant volume of solo content including battles and puzzles, both leading to various collectible rewards
# Simple, elegant interface for deck building and matches
# Matchmaking is usually swift (less than 30 seconds)

****Neutrals***

# Matches typically take between 5-20 minutes
# As with comparable games there are daily questions which if completed, deliver virtual currency rewards. With just over 10 hours of gameplay to date the rewards feel frequent and meaningful.

***Negatives***

# Personally, none to mention, but opinions will surely vary regarding the extent to which cash payments enable play advantages and are required to be competitive. I have no opion on this yet. It certainly does not appear to be significantly different to comparable games

review:
This isn't much of a VN, there are no bad endings, or at least any that I could find, and there's only one actual ending. But after 5 playthrough's, I have discovered that 99% of all text is generic and used for every character. The 1% being some flavour text in meeting a Romance option. 

If you are looking for a game where you can make choices to affect the story, you'll not like this game. It's linear, buggy, has no skip function beside "Auto", no option to increase text speed, spelling errors abound, I'm fairly sure the dev isn't a Native English speaker so I can't hold that against them too much.

The "Romance" characters are crap. They have no story, there's little to no interaction with them that doesn't have the same text as every other character. The only characters you spend time getting to know aren't even available to choose so you're basically picking "the prettest sprite" since the text is the same for everyone.

The story... oh god where do I start. I feel like they made a card game and then got drunk and tried to make a VN around it. The story is... dumb. I've played some pretty terribly written indie games, I test and correct grammar in more than a few every month, but usually they've at least put some thought into it. The characters sound like idiots and constantly change tone like they are bipolar and having and episode(Seriously, Nun told MC to "Shut Up" more than once then calmly started speaking again). 

The art reminds me of the old 90's VNs but with better graphics. That being said, the only images I saw were the avatars. There were no CG, no cutout scenes... it's just an amatuer on rails novela with pictures. 

2/10 - Try again.
