review:
This is a refreshing take on a match 3 game. It reminds me of ‘claws and feathers’ both in humour, look and how you see where and what item will be in the next move. There are 3 options but no timers/limited moves. Instead even here it’s different – easy, medium, hard with how many ‘enemies’ you will face in a round. Don’t worry there is no action or anything timed/reaction. The enemies are just things you can avoid while making your route for a round. That’s just one of the many variety of things that is different to the usual M3 games– you get a certain amount of tiles you can move in each turn and lives (depending on how hard you chose). Things don’t have to be grouped together, if there are 3 squares and 2 same items on the outer squares and your character goes through the middle you will get both items. You can get multiple different items in one go.

So the basic gameplay is different to begin with, then there are a lot of alternate game mechanics with its own rules so everything is kept fresh. There are bosses but still nothing timed, take your time to think what your best move would be. The bosses all have different moves with distinct ways to kill them. They aren’t difficult and even if you are going for all achievements this isn’t difficult at all, especially if you play on the easiest mode. But still just enough of a challenge to not get bored if going for all achievements.

I get bored easily but this was such a lovely change, the whole game it kept it fresh from the tile characters to what different things there were for you to do in a level and that was apart from having a different objective on each level. The level tutorial were clear and concise, easy to follow.

There are also in-game achievements, level map. One of the best games I’ve played in a long time, fun and great quality. The only negative is if you are replaying a level if you lost one of your lives, you have to go through all the level tutorial/story again you can’t skip it.

Recommend for all even if you aren’t a fan of match 3 games but are looking for a casual fun, quite relaxing game.

review:
S'allright.

I know that's not particularly helpful, but then again, this isn't a particularly deep game.

It is more or less a Match-3 game (in broad terms), where you must move your protagonist (a cat samurai) across a grid, surrounded by enemies and as you pass by or end up concluding your move sequence adjacent to a sufficient number of enemies, you will destroy them and remove them from the board.  Some enemies will randomly become "angry" and if you end your turn adjacent to them, they will injure you (and you only have a certain number of hit-points/hearts per level).

Obviously, as the dozens of levels go on, you will receive some special powers (e.g. a potion to quell all the angry enemies on the game board) that are each usable once per level, and some enemies will require two hits to destroy, etc.

There's even a few boss-fights with a variety of special conditions that you must contrive to bring about with your movement and attack patterns in order to beat.

It's not a terribly difficult game (on average difficulty.....there is a harder difficulty with less health), and I only died a handful of time over dozens of levels, and almost always on a boss fight.  The achievements are more-or-less easy to get and you will ultimately get almost all of them just through a normal playthrough (although there is one for killing a huge number of opponents where you will just have to avoid beating the level even when it's in your sights and deliberately stick around killing non-specified opponents rather than the ones the level wants you to slay, just so your can rack up a high enough number of kills).

So, it's certainly not anything special, but it's a fun way to kill ~8 hours if you're in the mood for a palate cleanser between harder, more intellectually demanding games.

Recommended.

review:
I dont usually write Reviews for indie games, but this "thing" rubbed me the wrong way a bit too much.

So what is "CADE PRIME"?

- A quadruple [b]Assetflip[/b] bunched together.
- It literally uses the demo levels of the Assetpacks linked below as the entire games content
- Green
- a complete mess


Assetpacks (Appear in this order in the game with pretty much zero changes to the levels themselves.):
1: https://www.unrealengine.com/marketplace/en-US/product/advanced-puzzle-constructor
2: https://www.unrealengine.com/marketplace/en-US/product/first-person-puzzle-template
3: https://www.unrealengine.com/marketplace/en-US/product/ultimate-fps-puzzle-kit
4: https://www.unrealengine.com/marketplace/en-US/product/puzzle-logic-system

1, 3, 4 have playable Demos on the store page, which is the stuff that is in this game. (which means, you can play 3/4 of the game for free, in way better graphics, if you really want to give this a go.)
2 has a video of what appears in this game, but in green: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=450TtZhl0Js


[h1]That aside, lets get into the other stuff that this game does not have:[/h1]
- A menu (Esc closes the game)
- Graphics options
- Sound options
- Keybindings
- Mouse settings
- Loading and Saving
- any artistical direction
- selfmade content

or to put it in different words: it doesnt even have the most basic functionality you would expect from any game.


[h1]The things the game has:[/h1]
- sometimes First Person Gameplay, sometimes 3rd person - depending on which assetpack you are currently playing.
- wonky physics
- a soundtrack which definitely doesnt belong into a puzzle game, but rather into a club
- red/green/blue boxes you have to move around... which you cant distinguish from each other because everything is green.
- a mix of different UIs, if there is one (each assetpack has its own)
- sometimes it has a crosshair, which is really useful when aiming
- different mouse sensitivities depending on assetpack
- the most basic puzzle gameplay you can imagine... because it is made up out of demo maps that were meant for developers.


[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
I stumbled upon this thing by accident, when I was scrolling through the store frontpage instead of playing Final Fantasy 14, like I should have been doing instead... would have saved me this "experience", but at least I can warn others now - so it has had something positive after all.

I played through the entirety of this thing and I still have no idea what the purpose of a game is that is made from Assetpacks that were given away by epic for free at some point and where the only content is the demo maps of said assetpacks that everyone can just download for themselves... for free.

Nothing in this game fits together, it lacks the most basic things, it looks like garbage in comparison to what the Assetpacks should look like... I just dont know who is supposed to play this.

[h1]I highly recommend to play any other (actual) puzzle game instead of this, its a waste of time. (If you really want to try this, get the free Assetpack-demos, they even look better.)[/h1]

EDIT: If you dont believe me, remember: you can refund within 2 hours of playtime or 14 days after purchase, whatever you will reach first.

review: At first, I would like to say that Cade Prime worth its price - only one buck, but don't expect anything really innovative. Cade Prime is not a traditional puzzle game like Portal or Antichamber. Instead you have to find some clues here and there. Sometimes it seems to me that it is more an exploration game than a puzzle game. There are some visual bugs, but the controller works well as expected. You start with some blocks to push in little rooms, and quickly you fall in a huge hangar which is really hard to solve.  In conclusion, Cade Prime is an interesting project for a while, but it needs to be improved by its dev team. Honestly, there is still a lot of work to be done ++

review:
This is the hardest of all the Laruaville games I've played with the new mechanics of having to move some things to different locations on a regular basis.  There are 100 "regular" M3-puzzle levels mixed in with a bunch of minigames (HOS, spot the difference, solitaire, mahjong).  The minigames appear so often it's more a mixed-genre game than a M3.  If you skip the solitaire and mahjong games enough times, the game will ask if you want to automatically skip the rest of those games, but the HOS and spot the difference games will keep on appearing and you'll have to manually skip them each time if you don't want to play any of the other content.

30 bonus M3-puzzle levels gradually unlock as you're going along, and these optional levels take the "puzzle" concept to a new level...I don't think I've even seen any levels in the Cursed House series which this developer also makes (that series has a reputation for being hard) which get to this level of challenge!  These extra-hard levels either feature black coins which must be avoided to prevent an automatic forfeit, or else must have things done in very specific order and parts moved exactly right to win.  When I first played Laruaville 10 at another site several years ago, I thought these levels were frustratingly difficult, but I've now come to enjoy the challenge.

The ghosts crack me up with their antics this time, and I'm still chuckling over Merlin the wizard living in what looks very much like a "cursed house" for most of the game until the other ghosts convince him to change his ways.

A nice enough game, played the other 4 in the series, each is a different gameplay style and this is a action bar turn based one, where each attack both by you and your allies/summon and enemies shows up on a bar, each side is only on one part of it so easy to read what action happens next.

It's not very long, about 6-10h for completion, have a bit more time as i left i on when doing other stuff.

Compared to the others in the series it's fairly easy, if you learn the rock-paper-scissor system you'll rarely die, if you click on the wrong type in the order you'll likely be oneshot but besides the clumsy missclicks you won't really die as the active battle system helps reduce damage (up to 100%) as the closer to the bars end the more damage you'll block in a risk/reward way.

You also get some Guard back depending on where the bar is and if you used the correct weapon type to block. (Ranged defeats Swords that defeats Magic that defeats Ranged etc)

Guard is a bit like armor and mana in one, consumed to attack and blocks damage to your hp bar, if you get good at timing and keep hitting at 70%+ blocks you won't be killed by anything besides bosses that needs bursting down.

Enemy attacks deal x damage, blocks reduce it by a % and you get a certain amount of block back depending on when you timed it you even get the leftover Guard to use if you did well enough. 

Some of the maps are a bit confusing but that's likely by design, (It has a cosmic horror/Hp lovecraft theme)  though one area will kick you back to the start of it if you walk in the wrong door so that's annoying when trying to explore and find weapons.

As of writing information is quite sparse so hard to look stuff up if you missed something, the optional bosses can be found near the end of the game, one in the library and the other 2 you need to go through a train.

Weapons don't unlock in the order of the inventory suggests, the last gun is close to the end but shows as the second slot in the inventory so that's a bit annoying.

[strike] Didn't run into any real problems so stable enough though one end game weapon from an optional boss didn't work for me, (final weapon in the sword type) but it's optional so got to the end well enough without it.[/strike]

Edit: it was supposed to work that way, with it not sticking around for more than one turn as it applies a status condition that can combo into a finisher (so a 2 turn kill on some enemies)

But overall it was fun enough and not very long so worth a try at least, would just take an evening or two to run through.

-I could not access the settings menu, even on multiple restarts and a re-install

-First boss room door has a step-through animation that glitched out and would not open, it made it so I could not do anything except float around even on a checkpoint reload forcing a completely new game

-Texture work, terrain, and lighting are all cobbled together and there are tons of glitches involving those

-Enemy animations are extremely minimal and I'm fairly certain most if not all are stock

-On enemy animations a lot are either too slow or too fast

-When hit the the sides of the screen glow bright red despite not being low on health, a few times it glitched out and the red stayed but was fixed on a checkpoint reload

-You have to jump to pick up ammo most of the time, and E which is the use button is also a quick-weapon swap button so if you try to use E to pick up the ammo you'll also swap weapons and sometimes pressing E doesn't even pick up the ammo

-Movement speed values are obviously messed up, a lot of the time sprinting will either cancel itself out for no reason and sprint-jumping can send you absolutely flying. There is also a bunch of collision issues

-Damage values are all over, sometimes enemies can barely nick you and the same enemies can also take more than half your healthbar

-Enemy collision is a problem, you can very easily get stuck on one enemy and have to kill it before you can move again

review:
Necrobouncer is basically what you’d get if you threw a goth rave in the middle of a roguelite dungeon and told everyone to fight for their lives. It’s wild. Pink Salt Games cooked up this frantic, rhythm-powered action game where you’re not just mashing buttons for the heck of it, you have to actually sync your moves to the thumping soundtrack. Miss a beat? Get smacked by a skeleton. Hit the rhythm? You’re a necromantic John Wick.

So, here’s the deal: you’re a necromancer bouncer (I know, right?) stuck defending an arena from waves of undead monstrosities. The story’s pretty much just background noise, don’t expect a Shakespearean drama here. It’s all about the vibes: dark, gothic, lots of pixelated blood, and music that hits harder than your morning coffee. Every attack, dodge, and skeleton-summoning move is locked to the beat, so if you’ve got no rhythm… well, good luck.

The gameplay is all about keeping up with the music. Each level comes with its own track, and that changes how enemies spawn and attack. Sometimes it feels almost like you’re dancing, if dancing involved frantic button presses and a lot of dying. The roguelite bits, randomly generated levels, permanent upgrades, permadeath, all that good stuff. So yeah, you’ll die. A lot. But hey, that’s half the fun, right? You keep coming back, trying to get a little farther, maybe unlock a new power or two.

Visually, the game is dripping with style. Pixel art, sure, but not the cutesy kind, think more Castlevania, less Stardew Valley. Everything’s dark, moody, and just slightly gross in the best way. The animations are surprisingly slick, and when you nail a beat, the game really lets you know. And the soundtrack? Man, it slaps. Heavy, haunting, a little bit sinister, honestly, it’s half the reason you’ll keep playing.

Now, if you’re not into games that kick your teeth in, Necrobouncer might not be your jam. The learning curve isn’t so much a curve as a brick wall, and some of those enemy waves are just unfair. Plus, the story is so minimal it might as well not exist, and the arenas could use a bit more variety. But if you’re down for a challenge and love games that make you move to the music, this one’s a total blast.

In summary, Necrobouncer is pure adrenaline for rhythm game junkies and roguelite masochists. It’s stylish, tough as nails, and does something actually new with the genre. If you like your games hard, your music loud, and your pixel art dark, go give it a shot. Just don’t blame me when you’re still playing at 2am, cursing at the beat.

[b]TL;DR - barely passable game at best with many problems, varying from major to minor.[/b]

Problems: 

[b]1)[/b]
Poorly optimised causing it to lag spike every 5 seconds. Not a big game or anything, and there are bigger games I can play on the same device with no problem.

[b]2)[/b]
Has an R18 patch... and still censors both gender's lower genitalia... Only breasts are uncensored.

I would say 'why did they even bother with the patch', until I remembered the game literally didn't work until it was installed. It just loops some obnoxiously loud music with a black screen aside from one small emblem in the lower middle of the screen. 

So, honestly, why have it as a patch, when it's needed to play the game and still censors most of the adult content?

[b]3)[/b]
The MC is the same, generic misogynistic prick who no one but those in jail for SA can possibly root for. 

No redeeming features, and also has other flaws such as an initial bigotry for the first monster girl. The fact that half the people seem to go along with his perversion too, just, wtf. (Note, oncoming sentence is hyperbole) Why isn't the author and people who approved such a character on a watch list? Don't know if this improves later on in the game, but, with this kind of character and those surrounding him, I very much doubt it.

[b]4)[/b]
It takes way too long to access settings, and starts at max volume. Without the r18 patch, as stated in 1, impossible to change. With the r18 patch, you need to start a new game, skip the introduction (for reasons in point 5) and get through the first cut-scene, just to skip the lower the volume outside of volume mixer.

[b]5)[/b]
The introduction, right now, crashes the game. You get to see the first monster girl in it, but when the second comes on screen, it crashes the entire game.

[b]6)[/b]
Most games like this save what option you picked in a fight last time, and starts there... Guess what, this game doesn't. Yes, it's defaulted to 'fight', which, to where I got, is the only attacking option. But, if you're trying to keep healing, or using items, you have to keep going there, which gets grating.

[b]7)[/b]
Translation is scuffed, to where half the battle text isn't translated.

[b]In conclusion[/b]
Overall, even with patches, point 3 is an automatic turn off for me. If you can deal with that, there is a chance the rest gets fixed in a patch, but isn't worth buying until then. As a connoisseur, doesn't really do anything new in the adult rpg maker-esque market.

From my perspective, there aren't any positives, the graphics are similar to other low-effort rpg maker games, has random holes in the scenery sometimes and the majority of every map is wasted space that does nothing but waste seconds of your life travelling through it. review:
I've had the luck of testing this game prior to release so I saw it grow and improve in the process. The final result, considering the speedy dev time of Terarin, is nothing short of amazing. Riding hot on the heels of the previous title, Raging Blasters (which I also recommend to try since it's very beginner friendly), Moon Dancer opts for a simpler approach, mixing the lock-on mechanic (with three distinct types of guided laser missiles) of titles like RayForce but adding a traditional coating to it, including checkpoints, which are a trademark of older era STGs. There also is a loose chaining system that (thank heavens) doesn't require stage-long chains from you as well as hidden items and some bonus enemies you can destroy for extra points. Your score and difficulty also determine que extend thresholds so it's a good incentive to get you to score well and obtain a good stock of lives to face the final stages.

Oh, and don't worry though: the checkpoints and stage structures are so masterfully crafted that recovery after death IS possible, unlike titles of that era and that, for sure, is an EXTREMELY welcomed change for those looking for a challenge.

The three difficulty modes are also fairly accessible but those not used to one hit deaths may still find it difficult. Nothing that some practice and stage layout learning can't fix. Most stages are fairly short but intense and very well designed in their enemy wave patterns to keep you engaged.

This is one of the most accesible STGs I have played in a while and that alone warrants a recommendation but the addition of an engaging and replayable Caravan Mode as well as an amazing OST (perhaps even better than Raging Blasters, especially the first stage theme!) certainly elevates the whole experience and warrants getting the game+OST bundle. Or you can head to Bandcamp and get it there too.

Specs wise, you won't need a superpowered PC to get it running, it'll detect an Xbox One pad straight out and running it through Steam Link to play it on my phone proved extremely easy although you will want a bluetooth gamepad in that case.

In short: very recommended!

review: Another solid release from terarin. The game is fun. The game in terms of mechanics has a minimalistic aproach. you have the directional inputs and a button. It may sound too basic even for retro game lovers but it works has the mechanics are elegant and the button has two functions that work pretty well. First functions is a multishoot (forward and diagonbals), second function is a lock on system like rayforce. there are weapon pickups for the lock on system and powerup pickups that increase the power of your shots(bot normal shoot and lockon). the lock on range depends on pick up. it may have a form of a small circular area around you ship or a square in front of your ship with sligtly more range. On rayforce you had a 2 level dimensional areas for the enemyes (one for normal shoot, other for lockon). In moon dancer you only have 1 area for both shoots. At first glance and by this description you will ask why you have the need of lock on system since a normal shoot has more range and always hits the enemy and here lays the elegant design that i spoke in the beggining of the review and i am going to explain now. to avoid this problem the designer made the elegant choice to have the normal shoot weak and the lock on shoot powerful. In fact normal shoot on is almost useless in bosses and stronger enemyes as it will take a long time to kill them. It is only useful on popcorn enemyes as you will be almost forced to use lock on. That game mechanic also increases the risk of attacking enemyes, as you  will have to attack at close range often. In that sense is a shmup that  relies a bit on memorization. To reward this risk you have a score system that will give points and cristal if you do multiple combo shoots with the lock on system. crystal will give you score at the end of the stage.The difficulty is low, but don´t expect the lower difficulty of other terarin games. The graphics may look primitive but they work well, because they are well animated and have a excelent bullet visibility (a trademark from terarin). i whished more games used this style. The music is good. The price is a bit high compared to other ofers in the market but ok. since it has  quality. I reccomend with a slight discount. Sometimes less is more and that is the case with terarin games. They are easy, they don´t have nothing mindblowing (but always good),but they have a fun, cohesive and unique aprroach to retro shmups without the problems of that era (big hitboxes, gradius syndrome, no autofire, etc). I strongly recomend this game.

review:
An artfully crafted narrative, with increasingly tedious gameplay. Music, menus, and visuals are all great and complement the game’s themes and atmosphere very well. In the beginning, the gameplay is rather simple and somewhat charming. It drags near the end of a first playthrough, around 12 hours or so.

While I think the story is fairly decent and worth experiencing, I cannot recommend anyone put themselves through experiencing it fully. The lack of quality of life features and tedious gameplay required to experience all this game has to offer is absolutely nauseating. You're much better off watching the endings on YouTube.

That's the short of it, now the long of it.

[h1] Story [/h1]
You play as Elise, a girl born under mysterious circumstances. You go about your daily life around town, learning more about the towns people and the world. Many mysteries occur throughout the story’s run time, which end up making no real sense and amount to pretty much nothing. It’s quite disappointing. The story is also highly predictable, outside the random shock horror mystery moments.

I was quite invested as all the mysteries and plot unfolded, but the ending(s) failed to capitalise on a lot of them, outside the main plot. For example [spoiler]throughout the game many weird rituals happen. Goats falling ill (and decapitated, but no one really seems to care about that...), a child disappearing, horses going poof. All in service of a priest doing a ritual. How this magician performs his wondrous tricks of moving horses in mere seconds, almost killing them for dramatic effect, etc., defies all logic. Where did he hide them? How does an old man, let alone anyone, steal a pack of horses? Why is the saddle thrown onto the pig? etc. I don't ever see these things get explained, but beyond this, all the new hooks on each passing day in the story revolve around this and the conclusion being "it's just a ritual LOL" is unsatisfying[/spoiler].

The main plot I found quite interesting, learning about the mystery behind Elise, [spoiler]demons[/spoiler] and what have you. Endings that elaborated on this, among lore drops here and there, were very engaging. Repeat playthroughs would probably be more insightful if the gameplay were not so monotonous. 

Also, gotta give the game props for making the town feel very alive. There are a lot of NPCs; while not all of them feel distinct, they all clearly have relationships to one another, gossip, and are written in a way that feels very *alive*. Every portion of the day they'll be in a different place, talking about different things, often in groups. Conversations with these NPCs are all pretty surface level, nothing too crazy, but I enjoyed them.

Worth noting all the romance scenes in this game are lesbians, which is a little strange considering the [spoiler]witch suspicion system[/spoiler]. I went for Freya, however, Leb is actually best girl. Romance scenes are written okay? Think Persona-level social links.

Overall, the main story was interesting; most of the hooks drip-fed in the story were disappointing, and town feels very alive. Everything outside of that was okay.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
Zoinks Scoobs, the gameplay. Gameplay has two sections, the puzzle sections and day-to-day sections. 

[h2] Daily Life [/h2]
The daily life sections all revolve around balancing arbitrary resources. Each hunger point decreases per time of day tick, sanity drains in caves, suspicion goes up and down from dialog choices. There is an attempt to interleave these systems, such as your party member is a big'ol' derp, so she'll raise the townsfolks' suspicion if you don't take her on chores with you. This costs you an extra 2 food points. There is a hungry gorl who will ask you for food daily, if you don't give her food, she chats shite around town and raises your suspicion.

Suspicion is raised as a punishment yet it is painfully simple to decrease. Walking around town and chatting randomly, you can talk to townsfolk and you'll get a dialog choice, usually a choice between "feck you" and "feck you (but politey)", picking the latter lowers suspicion, the former heightens it. In other words, the decisions are obvious 9/10 times. Which defeats the purpose of the entire system.

Mini-games are also present in these sections, which give you some amount of money depending on how well you do. Money is then used to buy food and sanity-relieving items. Mini-games are super simple but quite charming, like the rest of the game. They never outstay their welcome during a first playthrough, though there are only 3 of them, would've been nice if there were an extra 2 or so.

I don't think these sections are terrible, they just get repetitive and aren't engaging at all from a gameplay perspective.

[h2] Puzzles [/h2]
Every day you go to some [spoiler]psychedelic fever dream[/spoiler] area to do some basic puzzles. Near the end of the game, they do require you to activate some neurons to solve them, but not by much.

In terms of design, all areas look appealing and have a distinct theme. I was never not intrigued by what the next area would look like.

In these sections, you also have health; if you hit zero health, you die. Annoyingly, you get hit and die very cheaply in this game. You walk forward two paces and a twig will erupt from the ground and stab your pinkie toe. There are so many instances where it'd be impossible to dodge something your first time through an area. Instances like this are learnable, it's just annoying. Most infuriating is the instant kills that seemingly come out of nowhere. Such as the escort quest, which instantly kills you if your escort dies, but the game does not make it clear they ACTUALLY died, so that left me confused about why I was instantly dying. A boss section has a timed Q&A, you get one wrong, you must re-do THE ENTIRE BOSS and the answers are not obvious. One stealth section has masked dudes, who you can run into from the side of the screen; if you do, it's almost impossible to react without getting hit and teleported back to your nearest safe zone. 

All in all, just frustrating and cheap, not hard. 

[h2] The Big Problem [/h2]
The story is the main focus, but the gameplay is highly tedious. The biggest issue? No new game plus. All the game's systems are perfectly fine for a first playthrough, the game ends before they become irksome. The game has 10 endings and it's IMMENSELY easy to miss getting any of the good endings. I want to replay it, but without any new game plus option to easily skip scenes or jump to some point in the story I want, I don't want to invest another 20 hours to get 5 hours worth of story. They should really let you carry over items, relationship progress and let you bypass all the daily chores or puzzles to speed run getting the story you want. Without this, I cannot recommend anyone waste their time versus going to YouTube to watch the content you missed. It's quite a shame.

[h2] Conclusion [/h2]
A captivating story, nestled in tedious gameplay with a lack of new game plus to skip the boorish parts and experience the parts of the story you missed. As a result, the game wastes your time (especially if you get a bad ending), so it is hard to recommend in the end.

review:
Indie game feel + 80s shoujo anime inspired artstyle with some horror in there for good measure. Little Goody Two Shoes is a wild ride for 2D puzzle adventure fans. If the artstyle is drawing you in, let it and give it a shot.

Pros:
- Great story and characters, as the town becomes more and more paranoid of witch talk and gossip it's easy to imagine the characters falling for here-says strange noises in the night
- Beautiful art style, mood, sound design, and great use of lighting
- Level design relies on artstyle and lighting to help guide the player rather than relying on quest markers/pointers
- Romance feels believable between all the characters and not there to entice players

Cons
- English voice acting can be a little hit or miss, some lines are delivered a little flat or too angry even though the character portrait/model doesn't match. Would have loved it if the songs were also in English too similar to how 80s/90s anime would have dubbed anime openings. It feels jarring when the characters speak English, but the are supposedly singing on in Japanese
- Some deaths can feel very trial and error with the pitfalls and instant kills, which would be fine if the time between dying and when you can control your character again feels a bit too long. Maybe an option to skip after the first death in each new area would have been helpful.
- Was hoping that Elise would get more clothes/accessories as the game progressed giving you more advantages/disadvantages in the dream world [spoiler] This would also tie the game play and story together by having Elise/the player feel the need to collect more clothes to live the life she always wanted and yet shows off her vanity while making the townspeople more and more jealous/suspicious of her[/spoiler]

review:
Overall I liked the game but after the demo I knew what I was getting into.

That said:
Visuals are great, really like this artstyle, was a main selling point for me.
I feel the story is good overall. I like how weird it is and it's well put together.
I also liked the soundtrack.
The gameplay is tedious and annoying. There are a lot of problems with it. The town gameplay is repetitive and hardly matters at all. You go from a scene to a scene. It doesn't overstay it's welcome so it's not that bad, what's bad is that in those scenes the game ask you questions a lot. And their outcome feels random (cause this is a game where the character says a very different thing that what the choice box displayed and gives you no hints). This is a game that wants you to reload your save over and over and over again and remember how to respond all the time. The "choices" aren't divergence, they are just zero-sum, you either get them or fail. And the main problem of that is that the save system makes it very tedious (it's save points, so getting to the point you want or must repeat is often relatively long).
The game isn't hard, but it likes to take you by surprise and kill you, many deaths also can feel cheap. That said I didn't mind them much (mostly), it supports the horror vibes and in the puzzels/dungeons where they mostly occur the save points are more generous and easier to get to so that was fine. Here comes the main problem of this - outside of the dungeons you don't know WHEN the game will throw you into something that kills you by surprise (or just throws you a question you really don't want to fail), and sure that makes thing interesting but there are only 3 save points in the town gameplay. And the sequences are long. So either when something happens you lose like a half an hour to get back to the same point or you go save after every sequence which takes a minute or two every time to get there which accumulates to the same time loss overall. That's what is very tedious and annoying.
The game doesn't overstay it's welcome. It wraps itself up in a good pace manner. I didn't mind the mechanics nor even the cheap deaths, but the save system used here really sucks for this kind of gameplay. That design decision really hinders this game for me.

Overall like I said, after the demo I knew what I was getting into so I can leave a positive review. But If I'd come here blindly that would probably be different.

review:
It's alright. Soundtrack is a bit on the weaker side...I liked some of the tunes but a lot sound kinda bleh. It doesn't help that the guitar sample they use in every song sounds really bad.. Stages have sort of bland level design where there aren't too many stage gimmicks and a lot of the layouts are pretty flat. Most notable stages here are the shmup stages. There's two of them, and while they aren't that difficult by shmup standards, they're the hardest thing in the game by far and will probably filter at least a few people. Like for reference, they're about as challenging as some of the secret boss content in DELTARUNE (Not that deltarune is particularly difficult... but the shmup stages in Udongein X took me a similar amount of tries).

Bosses are kind of a mixed bag...there's maybe a 40/60 split between decent challenging fights and piss easy encounters. The characters are cool though, I'm personally not that familiar with most of the cast but fans that are more plugged in will probably enjoy the rep here. Unfortunately there aren't any special weapons or sub weapons. You collect little currencies from boss kills and as secrets in stages that you can spend in a shop menu for some upgrades. These upgrades are things like more HP/faster charge...but there are a few that give you new abilities that would be sorta analogous to what an armor upgrade in MMX would do. Regardless...it still feels a bit weird to be at the end of the game without any real visual or mechanical change to the character and how they fight. Well not that I know much about touhou, but I guess none of the characters really "grow" in the conventional sense like how X would? My friend makes it sound like everyone is just OP by default and the only thing happening is character's holding back instead of growing stronger. In any case I found myself wishing I at least got special weapons from defeating bosses.

That being said, I enjoyed the gameplay and thought the shmup stages especially were great fun. For only 5 dollars I think it's totally worth it if you have a MMX itch and wanna play something for an afternoon or 2.

review:
Stickit, when you play for the first time, will present you with a seemingly impossible task. Obtain the Golden Stick.

I initially thought this was going to be another rage game like Jump King or Getting Over It, but for some reason I don't find myself getting upset when I fail, and I think that is largely due to the fact that the controls are actually incredibly responsive and intuitive, every fall can only be blamed on your own mistake, and that will drive you to get better, and beat it the next time.

Learning each obstacle is a slow ordeal. Most of the time you can get away with using practice lamps, but other times there's no other choice but to turn it off and put all your hard work on the line for the sake of progress. 9 times out of 10 you will fail horribly, but every time you get just a little bit closer to the finish line.

It's very rewarding to discover new shortcuts to take, master them, and slowly get closer to the top. Obviously I'm nowhere near the Golden Stick even after 8 hours of trying over and over again, and I may never get it, but that rush you get when you finally beat that next obstacle only grows as you play. 

If you have $5 to spare on a game, you'll have an issue finding a better platformer to spend it on than this.
9/10 would recommend. Only issue is sticking to corners when jumping straight up.

review:
I've always liked puzzle games since even before Myst first came out. This game is just what it looks like, you move from room to room trying to figure out how to move cubes and other things to enable you to solve the room, obtaining (non-spoiler) "items", and figuring out how to move to the next room. 

Characteristics you may want to know before buying:
* This game is very abstract, no story at all. It doesn't need one.
* The game doesn't provide a mapping function, so you might get lost sometimes. You can always take screenshots if you have a hard time remembering whether you have solved each room before or not. 
* There are four main zones, and you can teleport to zones you have reached before, so you can go back and find any items you missed.
* Rooms reset if you leave a zone, though you keep items you have found.
* Color is important. As far as I know, there is no accommodation for color blindness.
* I didn't get all of the trophies, and I don't know what the missing ones are because there are no descriptions.
* I was unable to change the key binding from the standard WASD configuration. The options were grayed out. I was able to change other key bindings.
* I bought this for $7.99. It was worth the price.

Minor spoiler/complaint: 
A non-specific hint that I only figured out out of desperation: Just because one room doesn't let you do a certain movement doesn't mean all rooms prevent it. This is my only, minor, complaint - I expect a game like this to be consistent. On the other hand, it certainly made it more challenging to figure out how to get to some places.

While I must agree that the marketing and store page for this game is a complete mess, I must also be honest and say that the game is outstanding.

What we have here is... The GOTY version of Hitman 1 inside of WoA. That's it.
If you previously already owned H1 GOTY, you'd get this for free if you bought H3.
Now that H3 has been turned into WoA, you get this for free anyways when you buy it.

It means you get access to (in order of importance):
- The Patient Zero campaign, which is absolutely outstanding

review:
[h1]Experienced on the Meta Quest 2[/h1]

You can view my initial impressions review & gameplay here: https://youtu.be/DJJvBqQ0oBU

I wouldn't say this is a good game as is. I will say that I think it's got potential and it's got a good core gameplay loop. However, I did experience some major bugs. The biggest issue I faced was the sounds were totally borked. The sounds sounded feint and like they were at a distance. There was usually silence. Obviously, sound is very important in VR gaming so that is a big issue that needs to be fixed. I understand this is in Early Access, but that's a serious issue that can't be overlooked.

This is a roguelite FPS shooter with different seed levels you can select, along with degree of difficulty. You're a tiny robot on a hoverbike and you can fly around the halls of a space station as you hack, shoot, teleport, & gravity gun your way through & around enemies. You pick up ammo, scraps, & different hacks such as turning your enemy into an ally or putting them to sleep. Unfortunately, the gun feels like you're throwing spitballs because the bullet speed is so slow. 


Game is running on the Unity engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting mostly 90 fps. You do fly around in almost 6 degrees of freedom (you cannot pitch up or down). Movement feels very good and intuitive. The only settings available are for sound ... which are broken. I think the HUD is missing (Bug?) as that is shown on the store page video, but I didn't have a HUD in my gameplay.

Overall, I was having fun, but also, things were getting a bit repetitive. It was a letdown seeing the same drab looking space hallways over and over. I think I saw 4 different enemy types: a spider robot, a flying drone, a big sentry type robot, and a turret robot. I think the game needs more variety and maybe some different types of objectives. 

[b]Rate 5.5/10. I would only recommend this game for those wanting to support development.[/b]

When starting out, I recommend the non-timed one, and only trying the timed one later, once you get comfortable with controls and basic modules. review:
Poly Bridge 3 is the latest installment in the beloved bridge-building simulator series developed by Dry Cactus, and it builds upon the strong foundation of its predecessors while introducing new mechanics, enhanced graphics, and a fresh wave of creative challenges. At its core, Poly Bridge 3 remains a puzzle game that brilliantly combines physics-based engineering with lighthearted humor and a charming visual style. The game invites players to take on the role of an engineer tasked with constructing functional bridges that can support various vehicles, from compact cars to lumbering trucks, all while contending with a range of environmental factors and budgetary constraints.

One of the standout features of Poly Bridge 3 is the way it balances accessibility with complexity. The game starts with simple, intuitive levels that serve as an excellent tutorial to introduce the basic mechanics of bridge construction, such as the importance of tension and compression, strategic placement of supports, and the trade-offs between different materials. As players progress, the challenges ramp up significantly, requiring more intricate designs, clever use of hydraulics, and precise timing to accommodate moving parts like drawbridges or suspension cables. The physics engine is impressively accurate and consistent, making the experience feel grounded and satisfying; seeing your bridge wobble, shake, and ultimately hold or collapse under stress is a core source of joy and frustration alike.

Visually, Poly Bridge 3 takes advantage of modern hardware to deliver polished, vibrant graphics that maintain the series’ signature low-poly aesthetic while adding more detail, smoother animations, and dynamic lighting effects. The environments are varied and beautifully designed, ranging from sunny coastal roads to foggy mountain passes and bustling industrial zones. These diverse settings not only add visual interest but also introduce unique gameplay elements such as changing weather conditions or tidal water levels that influence how bridges must be built. The soothing soundtrack and gentle sound effects complement the visual style perfectly, creating an atmosphere that is both relaxing and engaging, even when tackling the most mind-bending puzzles.

The game shines in its level design and progression system. Over hundreds of levels, Poly Bridge 3 introduces new mechanics at a thoughtful pace, encouraging players to experiment and iterate on their designs. The introduction of hydraulics, in particular, opens up a new realm of possibilities and creativity, allowing for the construction of movable bridges and other engineering marvels. Players are often given multiple objectives to meet, such as minimizing cost while maintaining structural integrity or ensuring that certain vehicles can cross safely within a time limit. This layered approach to challenges keeps the gameplay fresh and caters to a wide range of player styles, from casual builders who enjoy creative freedom to more hardcore engineers chasing optimal efficiency.

Another major strength of Poly Bridge 3 is its robust sandbox mode and community integration. The sandbox allows players to build without constraints, testing wild designs or perfecting complex contraptions. More importantly, the game continues to foster an active and creative community through the Steam Workshop, where players share custom levels, challenge maps, and innovative bridge blueprints. This vibrant user-generated content significantly extends the game’s lifespan and provides an endless supply of fresh challenges and inspiration. For players who enjoy creativity and sharing, this community aspect is invaluable.

Despite its many strengths, Poly Bridge 3 does present a few minor drawbacks. Some of the later levels can feel frustratingly difficult, requiring trial-and-error and precise engineering that may deter more casual players. While the game’s physics is largely consistent, there are occasional moments where unpredictable interactions or quirks in the simulation can lead to unexpected bridge failures. Additionally, the game’s UI, while largely intuitive, can sometimes feel cluttered or overwhelming when managing complex builds with multiple moving parts. However, these issues are relatively minor compared to the overall polish and depth the game offers.

In conclusion, Poly Bridge 3 is a stellar addition to the series that excels in combining accessible yet deep gameplay, charming presentation, and a thriving community. It continues to capture the magic of bridge-building simulations by encouraging creativity, problem-solving, and persistence. Whether you are a longtime fan of the franchise or new to engineering puzzles, Poly Bridge 3 delivers an enriching and entertaining experience that is as satisfying as it is challenging. It’s a thoughtfully designed game that not only tests your technical skills but also celebrates the joy of creation, making it a must-play for puzzle enthusiasts and creative minds alike.

Rating: 9/10

review:
Witches of the Fourth 1v1, perhaps better known by its alternative title, The Hollows Chapter 1, was a unique and engaging multiplayer experience that I believe will seldom be replicated by the games industry in the years to come. Like it is so often in real life, many actions in the game will spontaneously and unpredictably lead to a quick death. Upon death, both players are prompted to choose between the two heroines, Hex and Jinix, this binary dichotomy presents a degree of certainty and familiarity while also serving as a likely allusion to the classic parable of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.

The game's movement systems are matched by few other multiplayer shooters. The teleport system, which allows characters to cross entire maps in a single blink, is unfettered by restrictive elements such as a distance limit or cooldown which may have been included in lesser titles. The character's attack moves are rapid-fire but inconsistently damaging, sometimes serving to slay the enemy in a single hit while barely touching the HP bar in another. This element of randomness allows for dynamic and interesting gameplay to evolve as a session goes on. The maps of the game, while similar in aesthetic, all have gameplay gimmicks and striking layouts that ensure that gameplay never becomes dull.

All in all, Witches of the Fourth is not a game for everyone; the dull-minded, slow-witted, or otherwise intellectually or physically inept will be unable to appreciate this game in its full magnitude, but Fareed Flgaming's offering to the 1v1 arena shooter genre is sure to please the most hardcore of competitive gamers out there.

The opening chapter plants the seeds for a story which rapidly grows and intertwines to produce an action filled conclusion in the third chapter.

review:
Let me start by saying I would EXCLUSIVELY recommend this to a younger audience, around ages 10 to 15 give or take. I can easily see a younger teen me sinking some hours in this just playing around, but as an adult I struggled to stay engaged with this and cannot in good faith recommend this to an adult. 
That being said, I think it IS a good game with a very sweet message; that it's okay to be different and that you're perfect just the way you are. This would make a fantastic gift to a child or teen, especially one with something "different" about them such as a physical disability, but I don't think the average adult would find this engaging. Review that said this would do better as a children's cartoon is spot on, it basically IS that but in video game form.

Pros:
- very nice art style; very cute and cartoonish.
- music is great, as usual. 
- main character is very customizable. Choose their name, skin tone, hair, hair color, clothing, etc. You can buy new clothes + find new hair styles & colors. You can also name and dress up the dog too.
- a very sweet story where you essentially play as a teen with a physical disability & navigate their day-to-day life.

Cons:
- minor glitches. Experienced double prompt overlay as well as getting stuck on ledges when using the flying mechanic (you can cancel out of this).
- fixed perspective can cause the camera & controls to be janky sometimes. This is particularly prevalent when using the flying mechanic as it sometimes makes the camera jump around. By far the worst part was during an episode where you control the dog and are made to do a platforming puzzle; the camera just loses it's mind when trying to position yourself. Overall I didn't have a lot of issues with the fixed camera, but it does glitch out occasionally. 
- This game feels slow and has a lot of "filler" stuff. After like episode 4, I just couldn't stop thinking about how much I just wanted to be done. It did become more interesting towards the end, but i think it sucks when you're like half way through and just want it to be over.

Overall.... If you're a parent and you have a child / young teen? They'd probably sink some time into this. 
But you as a like 30 year old? I'd probably pass.

review:
I'm sad to report I really don't enjoy this game. The long and short of it boils down to having no interesting mechanics with replay value and no meaningful story content. 

You play this kid's day to day, getting dressed in the morning, washing up, walking to school, sitting through classes sometimes, and each of these activities is accompanied by a mini game. The problem is these mini games aren't much fun, and you will never want to do them more than once or twice. 

Story wise, it's that age old cookie cutter bully plot where the protagonist has something about him that makes him different, bullies pick on him, kid finds he has some heroic power and saves the day, and now people no longer think he's a loser. The game tries to pass this message that you're wonderful the way you are, but the story is saying that you're only worthy of respect if you do something supernatural. It's fundamentally at odds, and it has no real depth or nuance.

Lastly, the game is way too restrictive. There's a small town in the game, but instead the game controlling in 1st or 3rd person, it has a fixed camera that aligns itself perpendicular to the street you're on, so you're usually always facing directly to a house 90 degrees away of where you're walking. It's very disorienting and unfun and feels like a waste of assets. Dressing up also feels restrictive, with only a portion of your wardrobe being available most of the time during school days. 

I want to like this game, the art style is adorable, but playing it just bores me.

"Village RPG" offers almost [i]nothing[/i] of what is advertised on the store page.

The most outrageous thing about it is the insane (regular) price of 21 bucks. Seriously, what is the "developer" smoking to ask for so much for a fake game?

The expansion itself is great. The new mega structures really change how the game is played. This is one of the must have DLC's
 Mass Relays are gained relatively early game and so long as you've got the economy to build and support them, they make defending the borders of massive sprawling empires easy. No more waiting years for your fleet to travel from one side to the other in a war or crisis.
 Quantum Catapults are gained around mid game and are just really fun to play with. They're good for when you've been boxed in and travel restricted by your neighbors, so long as you've a pulsar star within your borders to build one.

Orbital Rings are a fantastic addition allowing you to turn your fortress systems into and unbreakable bulwark or they can be used to augment your economic worlds. They essentially act like another starbase in the system but have unique upgrades for planets.

Of the new origins my favorite is Slingshot to the Stars. In place of guaranteed habitable world, you get a broken Quantum Catapult that is extremely cheap to repair, so you can get it up and running very early game, and a crazy stupid buff that allows you to expand your territory far from your borders for cheap influence cost.

The new subject specializations are cool too. You can now dictate whether your subjects are a military defender, research powerhouse, or energy/mineral harvester in support of your empire. Vassal and Tributary roles still exist and offer your subjects greater autonomy. Be careful with specializing however, as it puts different strains on your own economy as you'll need to share resource production to support your subject since said specializing neuters their own economic abilities in certain ways.

That's all I have to say. It's a damn decent expansion. The new traits, civics, events, etc. are all just icing on this cake.

review:
So is this a very neat idea for a tower defense? Absolutely! Its one of the freshest ideas I've seen for the genre in a long time! Does it execute it well? I'd have to say it doesn't. Theres also the fact my anti-virus caught the application trying to connect to the internet in a sus way which is.... not a great look.

In a tower defense a lot of the engagement comes from strategic tower placement and the thrill of barely staving off the waves of enemies until you're so powerful that nothing can get past you. Each decision is important and meaningful and you're aware of the choices you're making at all times.

In Quad Dice Defence this is sadly not the case. While yes the scrambling to build a tower out of the dice allotted to you at the time is a VERY good mechanic with some solid choices in there the rest of the game play loop doesn't get very engaging until around the 15th level. The game does cool things to spice it up by having new pathways appear (which can disable your turrets by bisecting them which is VERY cool) but the enemies that appear on the pathways (again I've only played up to the 15th level) always die in one hit from one die damage (the lowest damage you can do) and often only one pathway is sending out enemies at a time. This isn't very engaging on it's own let alone 40 mins into a game. 
It's absolutely possible to plonk one tower next to a goal and have it defend the goal easily without any assistance, there just really isn't any challenge or variety. Nor does it let you sit with your decisions for any length of time. Most of the first levels really only last a wave or two before being finished without any introduction of any new mechanics at all, leaving me with the only thing I'm mastering is turret construction.

Without any enemy variety and all the waves only having enemies that just die in one hit with no real moments that actually try to overwhelm you the game is painfully one note and boring when it has such a cool mechanic going for it. This game needed more time in other parts of it than just more levels. Have less levels, far less levels, and instead give more enemy variety, with ever expanding maps and more powerful enemies so that I have to actually sit with my decisions and so that I'm challenged and surprised with new challenges! In it's current state I could not reccomend it to you as it only gets slightly engaging after 40 minutes of playing and that's simply too long, it should have gotten to that point in the first 5 to 10 minutes.

review:
Just within the first ten minutes of playing this game, I've come across the following. I will still attempt to play through the entire thing. But these factors are major deterrents, in my opinion, as they really take you out of/away from the game.

Actual Errors:
- spelling & grammar issues, correct-tense issues
- MC says she sees herself "in his turquoise blue eyes", when guy literally has purple eyes
- MC’s asked to get rope – you can inquire or not, but even if you don't, next scene is still MC questioning guest’s “work”, which she wouldn’t even know anything about (or that rope was for work) if she hadn’t inquired
- guest’s speaking in paragraphs, the paragraph displays all at once, outside ‘speech bubble’; you cannot read half of it, & no way to scroll – you have to wait until next phrase, then check log
- guest’s not speaking (there’s just “…” or "?" in speech bubble), but mouth is moving (& for a while)
- MC says there’s somebody w/ sunglasses & facemask, but sunglasses are on head, & no facemask at all; you later know it was supposed to be worn, b/c MC later says “takes off his shades & the mask, revealing the beautiful, handsome face underneath”
- NPCs say they’ve found guest “dressed in all black”, but guest is clearly wearing white t-shirt
- in POVs for guests, it shows it’s going to be one guests' POV, but shows picture of another

Function Issues:
- saving game does next-to nothing - when you load, starts you over, or @ start of chapter – I’ve not once been able to save/load correctly
- every time you click save/load, takes you to 1st pg, rather than the pg you were on
- no setup/keyboard actions in options/menu - so no easy way to go thru/skip - even then, "skip" is just "skip to next choice", rather than fast-forwarding
- rather, if there are quick-keys, I'm not sure what they are - I've tried almost every button on keyboard, nothing has any action but "continue” 
- pop-up windows are a bit much (obnoxious – big/loud) - & there’re pop-ups to confirm everylittlething, even after selections’re made
- b/c said pop-ups, & .5s delay, you may accidentally click an choice/response instead of just "confirm" (which is the confirmation after you already confirmed) - oh, & you cannot click out of pop-ups, you’ve to click "x"/"confirm" (for 2nd time)

Playability/Enjoyment Issues:
- really over-dramatic/obnoxious reactions/actions sometimes - there's tropes, sure, but some of this’ just beyond that (since I can handle tropes) - & it's *very* repetitive
--- once, guest & MC’re running, she says “w/o warning, I lift up [his] legs & carry him. He’s even lighter than I thought” –what? haha – later, when she realizes he (also) knows her/name, “oh well, time to go home”, what?
--- as another review mentioned – “oh well, guess I’m the owner now”, “oh, must be a burglar, & I’ve got to confront him”, “that nice car arriving in driveway must be mob, & I’ve got to confront them, too” – that kind of crap is just the beginning – & it leaves you hoping it’s not as off-putting by end of game (time will tell)
- if you ever decide to leave or something – while you would think you run into a non-guest, or experience bad-end, even run into guest that’s outside (rather than in B&B) – no, you just basically quit game; & it’s the same-exact thing each time “I was on flight next day, never heard anything about grandpa, B&B, guests ever again” – not only does this make enjoying various endings non-existent, it adds to ridiculousness
--- when option for leaving (or similar) comes up, there’s only two options – you either quit the game (“game over”) or ignore whatever the plot-issue is
- the “strange, why does this feel so familiar?” plot-point is incredibly repetitive
--- she hasn’t lived there in 15yrs, yet every single person who “knew her when” says she hasn’t changed – nobody not only recognizes somebody after 15yrs, but not when the last time was @ 3yo; this adds to gravitas of plot-point, but also ridiculousness
- MC says she remembers days w/ grandpa at B&B very well, but is blank for months before leaving – he won’t explain why, even though she’s plagued w/ nightmares/depression since --- more ridiculousness, haha; not just comparison of what she does/n’t remember, but also general unrealistic aspect, & how most would’ve exp therapy, somebody would’ve told/explained, something – not just left dormant for 15yrs w/ nobody saying a single thing
- sometimes, it’s like the game cannot decide if the MC’s on vacation or running B&B; that’s not even talking about how overbearing guests can be on MC – granted, that’s clearly part of plot mystery – but the game def waffles between MC acting either/or
- chibi pop-ups (not-quite animations) that accentuate/animate a scene/event are also big/loud - but mostly just b/c they cover 80% of screen, covering characters you're trying to see. it should be either/or - either chibi pop-up be 100% of screen, so nothing else to focus on; or have it offset from main story screen/view 

I’m really hoping the mystery of the guests obviously knowing the MC when she lived there as a child is resolved/revealed reasonably, if at all. If I get to the end/ings, and that’s not the case, this will be an utter flop. Dangling a mystery-to-solve carrot to do nothing with it? That’s even more ridiculous as this game has been so far, which is saying a lot. I’d have to whole-heartedly agree that you have to go into this with an open mind, ready for ridiculousness. But, you should generally go into *any* game with an open mind – so this shouldn’t get any handicap just because it’s legit required before any enjoyment could be had.

As of yet, I *want* to like the game. I’m trying to stay positive and hope that the plot/twist isn’t just a fishing hook, and I’m just going to be left hanging at the end (especially with how repetitive the topic was). Until then, the game is cute, and I can see it being fun if not so critical. The art is great, though there’s a couple of spots where the angle/body-structure is a bit off (and off-putting), but that can easily be ignored for the art as a whole. The little chibi animations/pop-ups are done with significantly more detail/clarity, but there is something to be said for the prettiness of the rest. Each of the guests and their blush is adorable, to boot. I have been playing in English - I haven't played in the other languages, yet, but the fact that there are four language options is really nice to see - I would be interested to hear opinions of those at some point (if I don't get to play through them as well).

While *I* can handle this - for now - I know that most cannot. Especially these days, when every little thing is a world-ending problem. As such, as of yet, I cannot recommend this to most people.

PS, now that I think about this, this has a lot of similarities to 7’Scarlet, with the latter being done extremely well (one of the best I’ve seen). So, now I’m not sure whether to be upset that much of the plot is similar, or that it’s just done in a ridiculous and much-less-polished way? Referencing a gun, and a gun/incident in the past, and the one guy saying “I won’t let anything happen to her, *this time*”.. yeah, this is getting really familiar.

PSS, I'm basically gonna be out of text room soon. So, anything additional, I'll add as comments. But basically, just a lot to consider before playing this game. If you can get over all this, have at it. If not, please don't subject yourself to this, and/or just to subject others to your complaints.

review:
This is... Well... This is something else for sure. You really have to go into this game with a different mindset. I understand from the internet that later in game things get more serious but I haven't nearly reached that point yet. Instead I'm still at the point where I'm wondering what the hell is happening.

So far I've met a guy who is rich, arrogant and calls me kitty. And I've met a guy who is brooding and calls me Chihuahua. Because that makes perfect sense, ofcourse.

You start the game by thinking you will have 3 lovely months of vacation in your grandfather's B&B. Instead you're met with a note, saying you have to take over leadership while he spends 3 months on holiday in Europe. Oh right, and money is tight for everything so yeah, good luck.

You get several options (call grandpa and complain, turn around or embrace the opportunity). I chose to call him, phone goes to not available and MC goes like, oh well, whatever, guess I'm the owner now.
She welcomes her first guest by thinking he's a burglar and accusing him of this. Then a car stops outside and her first thought is it's the mob to take her with them and to grab a baseball bat to protect herself (what kind of life did she lead, seriously...?).

Dude number 1 pays for 3 months, rich guy pays for 3 months with an extra 0, 2 other guests join... But still apparently money is tight and the situation is difficult.

It also seems all of the people know her but none of them really admit it.

I don't know, it's not a bad game and the art is actually rather beautiful. I also love the pictures in between where the characters are drawn in a funny way to express how they feel. There's a decent amount of choices for you to change the story and I am interested in knowing what the mystery is and what happened that she can't remember.
I'm just a bit lost on how to view this game because it's so ridiculous.

So basically, yes I do recommend the game. But go into this with the mindset of 'let's have fun and go with the flow and take it as it comes.'
Because I'm still not entirely sure if I like it or not.

review:
I found this game because I am interested in Vietnam War games and this is the only Vietnam War VR game afaik. I was pleased by the positive reviews and the general "goodness" that surrounded this product. When I saw it was on sale, I bought the game and hopped in, expecting to be immersed into a low poly Vietnam War. Instead, I start the game, and am immediately thrown into a "tutorial" with no directions or even a dialogue, where I immediately get shot up and go to the main menu. Once in the main menu, I messed around with the guns, and noticed something interesting. [b] Some of the guns have weird hand angles (like the pistol) and all of them require the magazine to be inserted at the exact right angle. The guns also have NO HAPTIC FEEDBACK when shooting, making them feel like toys.[/b] I was also having an extremely hard time gripping the M1911 slide because I kept grabbing the wrong thing, even though my hand was over it and the "T" symbol on the slide was shown. The M60's top cover also rotates at weird angles when reloading, which just feels off. The mounted weapons shake side-to-side when shooting like they are mounted on jello, not a metal pole. I know sometimes indie games don't have super polished weapons so I put that past me and went into the first mission, Firefight. I enter, again with no directions, and my AI teammates start shooting at the enemies, who are extremely far away. I start making my way over to the enemies, dying a few times (they have really good aim after a bit of shooting) and eventually get somewhat close enough that I can possibly be expected to be able to hit a target using low-poly irons and my shaky hands that I'm holding out in front of me. I shoot them, but then get one-tapped by an enemy that I didn't see. I tried to reload while running, and my magazine disappeared when I put it in my gun. I tried again, and the same thing happened. After a few more attempts, I get frustrated and quit. I then tried the Gun Truck mission, only to be given the janky 1911 that is extremely hard to reload, and fail the mission.

TL, DR: I was extremely excited to play this game, but now I'm just disappointed. No directions and janky mechanics make this barely enjoyable. Maybe it'll be more fun in the future.

review:
Great premise, but doesn't really come together.  Some points:
1. Enemy turns take a very very long time and there is no "skip slot animation" option or anything like that. There is a LOT of time I spent sitting there watching the screen just thinking: "When is it going to be MY turn already?"
2. The tactics are muddy at best. Every enemy has an attack range of 2-3 and they can attack through your characters so positioning is almost meaningless. Enemies can even just jump over your units. Combine this with #3:
3. Lines of sight are really limiting. I can't attack someone in the square right around the corner? Meanwhile most boss attacks just go right over the walls, again making positioning meaningless.
4. I want someone who worked on this game to look me in the eye and tell me that enemy decisions are indeed random. Bosses always seem to roll reinforcements when they need them, and never do when they don't. Enemies basically just seem to do the optimal thing every round - which means the whole 5 seconds you have to watch each enemies' slot every turn is doubly lame.
5. Since your slots are randomized every turn, really the whole "slot machine" mechanic is revealed to be totally superfluous. Seems like it's only there for the singular purpose of randomizing jackpots, which are again obviously not determined truly randomly, since you never get them twice in a few turns, almost like they are deliberately spaced out, removing my confidence in any of the randomness, which is this game's selling point!
6. Abilities are all really samey, most classes play like many others, everyone's super move comes down to "do damage X number of times to Y number of enemies" except for a few characters.  Items don't really do anything interesting, they give very small buffs and influence your stats slightly, but there is so much room here for items to do interesting stuff like influencing your slot rolls or adding (the somehow only available on one single character) wildcards to your slots.
7. The final boss is total horseshit.  The combat is tuned with the sole purpose of taking your abilities away, you know those abilities you just spent the entire run developing? Yeah they're basically worthless in the final battle. Still, I beat him on the second try; the combat was more frustrating than tactically challenging.
8. $15? Get outta here this game should have been less than $10, tops.

I got a few hours of fun out of it, I might return to it from time to time, but I'm not sure it was worth it for me.

review:
Luck Be A Landlord sold me the slot machine, but ultimately left me wanting a bit more meat on the gameplay bone. Dungeon Reels Tactics delivers just that by putting the slot machine in a tactical combat roguelike. 

[b]Positive:[/b]
[list]
[*]I'm not nearly as much at the mercy of RNG as expected. Everything has [i]some[/i] gambling aspect, from party composition to rewards, but never so much that I think my choices don't matter. The worst reward roll is still worth something; the game could give you 3 duds, but you always get at least 1 gold. Recruitment gives you a choice of 3 random classes - maybe not the ones you were hoping for, but the abilities are fairly well balanced, so no party combo is a complete disaster. The global Jackpot meter gives you the option to save up the super ability for another character/turn instead of triggering automatically at 100 %. (Most super abilities involve 'do X to [i]random[/i] targets', so there's still an element of luck with them.)
[*]Many character classes with a good pool of abilities. Some are straightforward with attacks and shields, others have more unique abilities like teleporting or manipulating reels/symbols. Each also has a Jackpot ability that gets automatically triggered on 3 matching symbols.
[*]Unique take on 'Events'. The map follows the Slay The Spire structure with paths and nodes for Battle, Shop, Campfire; 3 maps, each with mini boss fight at the end, and a 'Heart' that can only be fought by unlocking the stage with keys. The Events are different from games that use this style of map though. These nodes have a selection of Fate Cards where you pick a boon/drawback pair - for example: sacrifice a stat to debuff enemies, lose gold to gain reward scatch tickets, take damage to heal a character of choice.
[*]The puppet show 'cut scenes' are funny, not too long, and can be skipped.
[/list]

[b]Meh[/b]
[list]
[*]I'm honestly over the retro style graphics, but that's a matter of taste. Sometimes it's difficult to tell similar-colored units apart on a crowded map though - namely green units between spiders.
[*]Relatively slow battle start because it takes a while for all units to plop into place. A faster animation wouldn't hurt here.
[*]Only one 'elite' enemy that can only be fought once. Makes sense since this fight rewards a key to access the final boss, and the other keys are obtained by other means, but some more 'elites' would have been nice. Having fewer but tougher enemies on the 2nd and especially 3rd map would also solve the issue of a long placement phase.
[*]Only 5 Ascensions. The difficulty does ramp up; I'm not saying 'meh, too easy' - but it feels more natural for a game like this to have 10 or 20 Ascensions, so the increase could have been spread out.
[*]Relatively long runs; 2+ hours on average, I'd estimate. Again an issue stemming from the amount of enemies, not the threat they pose. Oftentimes it just takes a while to mop them all up in their distant corners of the battlefield. I prefer runs under an hour, but that's also a matter of taste.
[/list]

[b]Negative:[/b]
[list]
[*]The one thing that really bothers me is how summons are handled. All bosses and some other enemies summon allies - and they get to act immediately instead of rolling for initiative like all other units. Most of the time, the summons are low health cannon fodder, but there's just something off about them acting in the same turn they were summoned.
[*]Little battlefield variety. There are different layouts, but they are all brown bricks with some green and white details. I can't tell if I'm on map 1 or 3; it all looks the same. 
[/list]

review:
Best way to describe this game is like flossing with paper. 

TL;DR Game does not explain its "unique" mechanics to you and leaves new players floundering in trial and error in frustration. Only becomes somewhat enjoyable at the end with all upgrades unlocked, but otherwise a painful endeavor. 

I am not an expert on fishing nor am I prolific with fishing simulators, but I have played a number of fishing related games and in-game minigames, with a variety of mechanics. This game by far has to be one of the most convoluted ones I have encountered, compounded by the fact it does not explain six out of the ten mechanics involved in fishing. It explains casting, adjusting lure, hooking (poorly), and reeling. 

However, it does not explain that you can overcast your line because your "distance" factor on your rod also effects the depth you can lower your hook and it does not explain that overcasting leads to the fish most likely breaking the line the instant you hook them. It also does not explain the "failure" mechanic as well, where attempting to reel outside the green zone not only does not help pull in the fish, but too many efforts to do so (indicated by the count down number next to the reeling bar) will cause you to instantly fail to catch the fish, letting them escape with your bait. Does not explain how you do NOT need to drop a fish's health to zero to catch it, just get it close enough to the dock, but also does not explain how "super catching" works and how it helps you catch the fish. It is not that these mechanics do not make sense, it is that they are never explained to you.

These factors had to be discovered by the player through trial and error, which is even further frustrating because failures literally cost you money since there is no "free" bait in the game. When money is tight and fish are not very valuable, each failed catch can set you back significantly and slow your traction in getting the upgrades that are rather costly. The explanations in this game are so poor I had to go to the forum to discover that to turn in the "paper" quests you get from the quest board in the village, you HAVE to do it in your little fishing menu. In the instructions it only says "you can see your quests" in the menu, and unlike almost any other game with quests where you turn it in at the board you got it from or are able to turn it in at the board OR in the menu, this game makes you go into your menu to turn in the quests, once again, never explaining that to you. I understand how some players complain of hand holding and how frustrating tutorials/explanation screens are, but providing even just a still image telling you what all the icons on the casting user interface that the player could bring up when they want to know or a optional tutorial NPC to talk to would be so much more helpful then letting the players flounder on their own.   

I can go on about how the fishing and delivery quests are annoying, the best way to make money is the little diving quests the villagers give you instead of actually fishing, how the "fish eating fish" mechanic makes sense until you realized it is based on species and not size which leaves tiny fish eating your big catches, and how the meager story offered tries to be funny but falls flat, and how the first female sprite you see has a idle motion that is almost exclusively her over-sized pixelated chest bouncing (which, if generously interpreted, is the developer's attempt to be "funny" and "ironic", but considering this character has no speaking lines and no comment is made regarding it, comes off as failing to be satirical at all at best and gratuitous and self-indulgent at worst) 

I do not recommend this game to anyone except maybe masochists and those willing to spend the first two hours of a game grinding their teeth.
