review:
I LOVE THIS GAME!!! MY FAVORITE GAME I HAVE PURCHASED ON THE STEAM SUMMER SALE!!!

However, I am having a MAJOR ISSUE!

While the game ran fine for me last night at a solid 30 FPS in 1080P and I was enjoying it thoroughly, I just woke up to what appears to be an AMAZING VISUAL OVERALL!!!

Now, on to the issue. The games graphics are now glitched on my hardware and my SAVE FILE GONE!!!

Heartbreaking!!

Is there any way to roll back to the previous version, prior to the visual update?

Also, is this game getting better optimisation for the Steam Deck in these updates?

The game runs fine for me at 30 FPS at 1080P but took some tinkering last night to get it that way! Low settings, of course!

I have 4 hours of gameplay, now lost!! That is a bit upsetting, but I do appreciate this Developer a TON of making this sort of game from my childhood!

I WILL BE BUYING THE SWITCH 2 VERSION ON CART!!

PLEASE FIX THE ISSUE ON DECK!! I HOPE MY SAVE FILE ISNT TRULY GONE BUT IF IT IS THEN ITS NOT THE END OF THE WORLD!

UPDATE:

Changing over to the Legacy branch appears to allow the game to run on the Steam Deck, however my previous save was sadly gone once the Developer switched over to the free Enhanced edition, and the game somehow runs rather poorly (very low FPS when in 720P and the game wants to output to 480P upon  boot now). 

Some things I wanted to let the Dev know about before porting to the Switch 2: in the Legacy version, the games enemies would sometimes go into bodies of water on accident and start following you. Putting some time of invisible barrier in place should prevent this glitch from happening! Also, this is a very minor detail but also adds a bit of flair to the overall oldschool aesthetic, but adding a button prompt after character dialogue, especially during the intro and cutscenes, and automatically setting the speech style to slow may help people to better understand whata going on, rather than just zooming past all of the dialogue without the average person being able to comprehend the backstory. Just trying to help out a bit! Minor details but they go a long way! :)

EDIT EDIT:

Upon collecting the first Fishy in Sweety's Spaces, I noticed that there was no collectable animation, which could help gamers to understand the task of collecting Fishies as the main task and add emphasis to the importance of the main collectible in the game! Such an animation would make this task also seem as epic as an achievement as obtaining a Fishy truly is! Just a little feedback to help out!

Also: I am quite enjoying playing this even though it is running at 480P 30 FPS on my 4K monitor via the Deck. In a very strange way, it gives it an N64 charm! 😂

Furthermore: This gives me an idea!! Perhaps add a secret "Nintendo 64" or "64-Bit Mode" in the video settings, which would essentially set the resolution to 480P, make it run at 30 FPS, and bumps the graphics back to Legacy (if possible) and enables a classic CRT filter over the top of the video, in order to give it that N64 look! Also, perhaps also make the game run at either 4:3 mode or toggable widescreen if you want to take it a step further! :)

OTHER IMPORTANT TWEAKS:

Character and enemy collision could use a bit of tweaking to its code, particularly referring to the bouncing of on enemies by our hero character friends! Maybe perhaps making the jump off of an enemies head a bit higher to give it more of a bouncy feel, preventing accidental collisions from happening and character health taken away.

Speaking of health!!

A simple tweak to the way that hearts spawn after defeating enemies can go a long way to making this game a pleasant experience for all! Ensuring that heart pickups remain on ground after enemies are defeated can go a long way!

Fishy amount on menu screen:
The Fishies deserve to be prominently displayed in the menu screen, alongside the 64 Carts, as this is the games main collectable! I would recommend, perhaps, therefore placing it above the 64 Cart in the menu system, so that we don't have to go through the Worlds totals and end up manually counting them all.

Guidance implentation for Yolkie:
We have this little flying friend here and it would be lovely if, when a button is pressed, Yolkie will start flying in the direction of the closest Fishies, then N64 carts after Fishies are all collected! Think Sparx in Spyro!

ONE LAST THING!
The world selection in the menu is fine for testing purposes, but I'd like to see this debug feature removed in the final product, as to encourage exploration of the huge beautiful hub world! Think Banjo-Kazooie. Some might think of that as going backwards, but it helps to keep that oldschool feel you're going for! 

I also clipped through the statue in the Hidden Temple after collecting the Fishie there. Just a friendly heads up!

Another thing of note:
HDR is broken on the Steam Deck, resulting in funky neon graphics! Turning HDR off fixes the graphics on the Deck, but performance, as mentioned above, is very poor and the game resorts to 480P to compensate. The main branch also has glitchy artifacts on the ground that I experienced right away in the hub world when testing.

I've also found that Ratties Lair dips in frames even running at 480P on the Deck.

Found another glitch wherein I got stuck between the Portal and the wall in Gingys Glacier.

And these are just some of the minor little bugs or glitches I have found in the Legacy edition! Hopefully I was able to offer some new insight into bugs or glitches that can be ironed out and features that could be added into the final product in order to make it a pleasant experience, especially on the Switch 2! Until then, I'll be awaiting its release on the Switch 2, and I'll be picking this up both digitally and physically upon release!

It's a mess.

As someone who grew up using Windows 98, and someone who wanted to try out at least one "survivors" game besides the OG Vampire Survivors, I [b]knew[/b] I had to try out this game as soon as I saw it!

Both the demo and the rest of the game are pretty good! I LOVE the aesthetic of the game - it NAILS the Windows 98 feel. And turning Clippy into a Sword is just brilliant. The game-play itself is pretty fun, with different enemies to deal with and many upgrades and weapons to collect and unlock. And I personally really like how we use the [b]mouse[/b] to dodge the enemies instead of the arrow keys or game-pad.

The bosses are pretty tough, though. You will need to grind for a while to get permanent upgrades to be able to stand a chance against them!

review:
I spent 4 hours into Desktop Survivors 98, which is kinda surprising for a simple game.

It's straightforward roguelite shooter with a nostalgic Windows 98 theme, using your wallpaper and application UI as the dungeon background. The main draw is nostalgia, with enemies and allies inspired by Windows 98 apps, menus, wallpapers and icons.

The game didn’t start off smoothly for me. When beginning a new run, I struggled to figure out where my character was, as the only UI was a frame on the sides. It turns out you need to pick a door to open on the side, which then reveals a full UI for either a battleground or an event area.

The gameplay is simple: fight or dodge enemies, collect experience and gold to buy new attack patterns or upgrade existing ones. Depending on your character, you’ll encounter classic Windows 98 elements like the Pipe and 3D Flowerbox screensaver, Solitaire 98, Windows Paint etc as your weapons. Enemies include variations resembling Clippy from Microsoft (man, I miss that guy. Also miss Kaka, the little lion from Kingsoft AntiVirus).

Weapons can affect a bigger range or higher damage after upgrading, the Flowerbox grows bigger, while Solitaire adds more decks. The fun part of the game is watching the actions, and when a weapon gets corrupted, it changes attack patterns, like Solitaire will start shooting decks from the center.

I’ve completed the game multiple times and unlocked all available dungeons, but a few characters remain locked. The menu keeps the nostalgic vibe, and there are mini-games to boost your default attributes.

I hope developers will consider adding a God Mode cheat after player had a few successful runs, for easy watching the battle, like many players did in Plants vs. Zombies.

With 81% of achievements unlocked after 4 hours, I’m quite happy with the content. I’m not saying the game itself is groundbreaking, but kudos to the developers for choosing the perfect theme and targeting the right audience.

Bitter Glass is the second game in the developer Daniele Doesn't Matter's "Scary Shadow Spot" series. This series is inspired heavily by the 1960's Twilight Zone TV show. + The "Getting Drunk" to calm your nerves, and "Throwing up" to get sober, gameplay mechanic is hilarious.
+ The story is mysterious and exceptional. Lots to uncover. Many interesting zombie characters to discover and talk to. 
+ The game is extremely polished, ran perfectly on max settings.
+ The AI voice acting is well done, very clear, and well written. It works perfectly to tell the story coherently.
+ Excellent creepy sound effects throughout the whole game.
+ Several really original and fun puzzles to complete.

- There are 2 puzzles in the game that rely heavy on trial and error, they can be super annoying, requiring many tries.
- Several times a woman ghost will chase you and you will not know where to go, run into the wrong building, and get instantly killed. Fortunately this will only put you back a minute or two, remember to load up your most recent Autosave in the main menu. Do not click restart, it will set you back further.

An atmospheric horror puzzle game in a western setting, who can say no to that?!
Overall: 8.5/10

[h1][i]HUNTED[/i]: Barely Functional, Barely Anything.[/h1]
‎

Considering that both the developer and publisher, fittingly named [i]Trash_Games[/i][b], [/b]have nothing else under their belt, that should probably tell you everything you need to know.

[b]Achievements: [/b][i]No Achievements.[/i]

[b]Recommendation:[/b] [i]Do not spend your money on this, Absolutely not.[/i]
[hr][/hr]

[h2]Story.[/h2]
[list]
[*]The store page doesn’t bother with a proper story synopsis, just the bare minimum: [i]“You wake up in an unknown place and try to escape from a maniac with a chainsaw.”[/i]
[/list]
[h2]Gameplay.[/h2]
[list]
[*]On it's store page, it's described as a minimalistic third-person horror experience, built around a simple premise and a no-save structure meant to deliver a short but intense, run-for-your-life style challenge. What you actually get is a barely functional mess that [b]struggles to operate past the first few minutes[/b]. The game is fundamentally broken, making it almost impossible to progress. What little I can say is that it's third-person, but even the most basic mechanics are awkward. For example, when you pick up a knife, the character [b]aims it like a gun[/b]. And when you finally get an actual firearm, it’s [b]weirdly offset to the right side of the screen, [/b]which might be an ultrawide issue to be fair.
[/list]
[b]Difficulty.[/b]
[list]
[*]The real challenge in [i]HUNTED[/i] is surviving its broken controls and game-breaking bugs. The hardest enemy is the game itself.
[/list]
 https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3503893227
[h2]Visuals, Audio, and Performance.[/h2]
[b]Visuals.[/b]
[list]
[*]The game is clearly built from cheap assets, with bland textures and environments that fail to promote any feeling. The character model is okay enough, but with awkward animations. 
[*]They seem to want to highlight that the protagonist is in their underwear, which is as far as it goes (for those that care), something the store page makes a point of mentioning.
[/list]
[b]Audio.[/b]
[list]
[*]The [b]footsteps are distractingly loud, [/b]a constant [i]clack-clack-clack[/i] that sounds like the protagonist is wearing heels despite being barefoot. So it's hard to actually notice anything else. And then there was the death screen, which hit me with an abruptly loud screech. 
[/list]
[b]Performance and Bugs.[/b]
[list]
[*]The “trailer” sets the tone perfectly by showcasing nothing but a [b]low-FPS mess[/b], so you kind of know what you're getting into. That said, credit where it's due: the game [b]does manage to run at more than 15 frames per second.[/b]
[*]The game’s biggest issue kicks in the moment you pick up the [b]knife[/b]. If you try to use it, either by equipping it or pressing the space bar,[b] [/b]your character just [b]freezes in place[/b], completely unable to move. [b]This kills all progression[/b], since the very first enemy ambushes you from around a corner. You're supposed to mash space to escape the grab, but because the game locks you up, nothing happens, and you just die.
[*]The UI that doesn’t even include a [b]quit button[/b] (yes, you have to Alt+F4 it).
[*]No resolution options above [b]1920x1080[/b], but surprisingly it [b]fills ultrawide without black bars[/b], so that’s… something, I guess.

I spent 12+ hrs of my life that I'll never get back thinking it would get better, but it just got worse. review: This is a super early reflection but I just want to touch on some points because this game certainly deserves some attention. I grew up in Montana and in my youth, had a very strong love of anime and anime tropes. Games such as Wild Arms, Boot Hill Heroes, Westerado, and something like The Real Texas are that niche genre that are my wheelhouse. I've always had a love for that clash of atheistic, and when I heard of this game a while back I threw it up on my wishlist without a second thought, this was going to be something special. The mechanics and minute to minute gameplay are similar to what you might find in the Evolution games for the Dreamcast/Gamecube. You got yourself a hub town and you got yourself some dungeon delving, go out and grind. So far it has been a lovely experience, especially at the price point. The graphics are done in a voxel style which I've always been a big fan of so if you like the charm that has to offer you'll be on board. So far my only request to the dev would be to please put an auto-battle feature. The combat reminds me of a Dragon Quest or Earthbound and I think it could really help the whole of the time spent, since grinding is so needed to have a feature such as that. If you enjoyed Boot Hill Heroes, if you enjoyed Wild Arms this is a unique opportunity to pick up something else that has that same panache but with its own twists. review:
[h1][b] A challenging hack-and-slash precision platformer where you willingly hurl yourself into deadly spikes [/b][/h1]

[i]SwooshCat[/i] has little real narrative; its only goal is for you to conquer a pure, brutally difficult pixel-art platformer.
Like most platform games you clear stages using dashes and jumps, without built-in double-jump. Instead you must earn extra airtime by bouncing off items or defeated enemies. Another twist: many sections expect you to dash straight into spikes and use them as part of the solution. Sure, there are other platformers where you ricochet off spikes with a weapon, but forcing a one-hit-kill character to physically slam into spikes raises the challenge to a new level.

About a hundred base maps (plus a handful of hidden maps) get progressively harder and more stylish, so simply clearing each stage feels fantastic—after countless deaths, of course. I finished the game with a gamepad first, then tried keyboard-and-mouse for a bit; the latter is far more precise and makes the game noticeably easier. If tight precision platformers wear you out, I recommend the keyboard-mouse combo. (After ten hours on a gamepad my hands were trembling—pretty sure I shaved years off gamepad's lifespan!)

[h1][b] Stunning level design & the magic of slow-motion [/b][/h1]

Within the precision-platformer genre, this game stands out for:
[list]
    [*]A carefully tuned slow-motion speed that just feels right.
    [*]Increasingly complex layouts (Jungle → Desert, etc.) that make you stop and think.
    [*]Limited slow-mo charges that force you to choose exactly when to use them.
[/list]
Because of these elements, the harder the stages get, the more the game turns into a mix of platformer and puzzle: you’re constantly solving “How on earth do I get from here to there?” rather than blindly jumping in. It’s a great reminder that, in a true precision platformer, the first move isn’t to leap—it’s to figure out the route.

[hr][/hr]

review:
[b]Village Tale[/b] is a cute little pixel-art idler that plays like [i]Rusty's Retirement[/i] if Rusty were building a wee village instead of a robot farm.  It hangs out above your taskbar, and manages to be interesting without being distracting  -- so, basically, it's the perfect workday idler.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
[b]Controls.[/b]  100% mouse (even navigation uses the scrollwheel).  It did not recognize keyboard or controller input.

[b]Gameplay.[/b]  Standard capitalism idler: Place resource-generating buildings, sell goods, gradually earn money, and slowly level up to unlock new items/work stations.  

[b]Playtime.[/b]  It took ~20 hours of occasional interaction to unlock every area, place and upgrade every building, and score 50 of 54 achievements.  I'd estimate another ~10 hours to 100%.

[b]Settings.[/b]  Settings include standard sound sliders, plus options to move/shift/shrink the game window above your taskbar and an option to keep the game on top of other screens.

[h3]What Works For Me[/h3]
✅  Large selection of background focus music.
✅  Toggle to automate order handling/fulfillment.
✅  Limited customization options for buildings and townies.
✅  Decor options include a full graveyard set, which: yay.
✅  Buildings can be moved at any time.
✅  There's a minigame to haggle with customers.
✅  Solid sense of progression.
✅  DLC lets you add cats and dogs.

[h3]What Doesn't Work For Me[/h3]
❎  The full map is too small; I had to cram the last items in.
❎  Production metrics are not clear.
❎  No, seriously, is the restaurant using wheat?  Pumpkins?
❎  I'm done decorating/upgrading at level 178; max is 300.
❎  Crop fields are often empty; I wish farmers were more active.

[h3]Final Thoughts + Recommendation[/h3]
Left to my own devices, I'm easily bored and more easily distracted; idlers and YT lofi channels are the only reasons I remain gainfully employed.  

[b]Village Tale[/b] isn't doing anything new, but it expertly balances player interaction and management with automation and simple mechanics; it'll do its thing regardless of whether you're actively playing or looking at spreadsheets.  I've enjoyed checking in on my villagers, micromanaging stars, and occasionally decorating between meetings.  Also, the soundtrack is top tier productivity lofi.

If you're desperate to relive [i]Littlewood[/i] or actively build a town, this is not for you.  But if you enjoy [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2013730/Gourdlets/?curator_clanid=45365863]Gourdlets[/url][/i] or [i][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2666510/Rustys_Retirement/?curator_clanid=45365863]Rusty's[/url][/i], or just want to watch little pixel people do their pixel people thing, then I can't recommend [b]Village Tale[/b] enough.

- clearing a number of lines, double or even triple lines
- placing a number of tiles on the board
- reach a certain score

- destroy block range 1 or 2
- place a single dot
- remove your last played tile

Every world begins with lighter goals, to gradually build up the requirements. So you can have an 'oof-moment' there.

review:
Game is somewhat okay with basic rts mechanic (Playable)
I would argue this game is in early concept prototyping stage.
as long AuroraDawnGames continue develop it and add touch up with sensible art style than within years the game can be finished as complete product.

Main issues are box selection algorithm, UI, camera, inconsistent unit movement speed and voxel art limitation.

a) Box Selection Algorithm 
Box selection algorithm now heavily favor building due to bigger hitbox (Unreal Engine Voxel Art Limitation).
So whenever you box select / manual select units near building, algorithm will always select building.
Dev will need to make building selection algorithm more tight and better feel.

b) UI 
Maybe because of UE default menu blueprint template, resource tabs are in the build menu (when building cant see resource). 
Location of build menu is at top right which is awkward, I suggest AuroraDawnGames to separate resource icon to top screen
and move build menu to bottom right (at bottom right like traditional rts).

c) Camera
Another issue will be camera angle, speed and movement control
I understand to make voxel art look good, camera need to be tilted or in angle.
However the current camera angle make it hard to see terrain (whether is it a slope or flat land), unit and enemy.
(24-05-2025 added) Suggest adjust camera angle to top down view like traditional rts (with slight tilt / ortho view  whatever they call)

For camera speed, I suggest dev to fine tune camera speed setting from straight slope to higher speed bump. (camera should move fast but with slight speed bump at the end, something like a tilted F shape)

Currently, there is no drag pan in the game and the current edge pan is too sensitive. (I believe drag pan and custom setting can be easily added to setting menu in the UE engine)
Also please make camera higher. (current camera is even smaller than old warcraft 3 zoom out when released)

d)  Inconsistent Unit Novement Speed
Unit movement speed is inconsistent. / weird movement logic.
Dev need to tweak the game engine movement logic.
currently all units appear to be floating and slight speed boast when select movement towards buildings or attacking.
When order unit to attack, unit will move around despite in range to attack. (for example, archer & crossbow will strafe left and right despite enemy standing in front hitting them.

e) Voxel Art Limitation /  optimization
From the setting, I can see that AuroraDawnGames understand UE engine render data storage limitation for Voxel Art (character limit set to 1000).
As expected, when I reach mid game with 800+ units, game become a bit laggy and sfx/effect no longer display properly in lowest setting.
I will argue some of the later level enemy units have too much details and can be further simplified (if voxel art is the final art style).
I am not art person but I believe there must be way to optimize the voxel art data storage limitation just like how other games with similar voxel art can do (more than 400k+ without any post processing)

Also please don't introduce any shader or post processing effect in near future (or allow player to completely disable them).
Late game will be unplayable if any shader is introduced for this type of game.

review:
These reviews are extremely misleading. I'm not sure if they're paid-for reviews or what, but there's no way hundreds of people think this game is worth $6. (The lack of discussion of the actual gameplay should have been a red flag... as, in retrospect, is someone calling this "the best blacksmithing game of all time" which is absurd).

First, this is a free browser game you don't have to pay for to play. I wish I'd known that. The only apparent difference between this and the free version is apparently a "favorites" bookmark system, which is an insane thing to charge $6 for.

Second, there's almost no gameplay here. Even if this were a ported mobile game it would be shockingly bare bones. The bulk of the gameplay involves stacking pieces as precisely as possible, something annoying on a mouse and near-impossible with a trackpad. Once you finish stacking pieces, you wait a while, and then find out if you have different-looking pieces to stack or will just be stacking the same ones. There is occasionally also some clicking and dragging.

And... that's it. It never gets more interesting or complicated. There's no automation, so you have to play through the same inane stacking minigames over and over. And then you sit and wait while an autobattle happens, and then it's back to stacking.

You should not pay money for this. Even as a free browser game, it's boring and pointless. As a mobile game, it wouldn't hold anyone's attention. review:
This is what I would consider a "physics puzzler," similar to games like iO, or Ink. Not an incredibly long game, but the first to last level (54 of 55) is a bit difficult. Not sure how long it will take me to beat the last two levels, but I've only spent around 90 minutes on the game so far. There is also a rating system for each of the levels--measured in "circles." So if you're a perfectionist you can work on getting three circles for each level. Though, there is no indication of how many clicks you're allowed for each level to get the highest rating, and the difficulty is a little inconsistent. The game does a great job of a theoretical difficulty curve, with the gradual introduction of new elements and orb types, but I've hit three circles on several of the levels in the middle of the pack without trying, whereas the early levels I've actively worked toward getting the highest rating, and just can't do it.

Nice calming music. The orb sounds are oddly soothing and ASMR-like.

There are some interesting concepts for the levels and mechanics that force you to really think about where you have to click to collect as many orbs as possible. Each orb type has its own specific physics, and the later levels introduce elements that change the behavior of the bouncing for each type of orb in addition to the orbs interacting with, and bouncing off, of each other.

I've been playing the game on my Deck. It runs okay, but could use some optimization. The later levels inexplicably tax the system to the point where the fans kick up and the battery starts to drain. Would be a great mobile game. My wife wasn't interested in it until I showed her that she could touch the screen to place the black holes to capture the orbs, and after that she was hooked.

Overall, it is a fun experience, but could use a little refinement.

review:
Right off the bat, let me tell you that Neko No Sentouki is a wonderful visual novel with a lot of passion, love, effort and dedication poured into it, which you can clearly feel every step of the way. There was someone here who really had a story to tell and deeply cared about not only their characters but also the craft itself.

Does that mean it's perfect? No, but it's a memorable ride from beginning to end, that got me emotionally invested and is sure to stay with me. But let's dissect it in a bit more detail, shall we?

[b]Story[/b]

It’s told from two very distinct perspectives, one of which you can choose at the start:

On the one hand, you have Hikaru, a seemingly grumpy and cynical young man living on the streets and getting by as a thief. And on the other hand, you have the very cheerful and naive Aiko who possesses superhuman abilities and takes part in a mysterious fighting tournament.

By chance, the two of them meet and their fates become intertwined as they make a deal to further their individual ambitions.

For most of the game, the overarching plot revolves around the tournament and the questions relating to its contestants, organizer, purpose and Aiko’s reasons for participating in it. There is a lot of mystery involved, especially from Hikaru’s perspective, which is why I’d recommend starting with him, as he (like the player) is the one getting dragged into all these things Aiko is already familiar with (although that doesn’t mean there isn't anything in Aiko’s route, which would benefit from choosing her first, so ultimately, either order will provide some unique surprises).

Now, while it was definitely intriguing, I do have to say, however, that the tournament plot, for the most part, was pretty simple if not generic. But that’s fine in my book, because what really kept me engaged were Aiko and Hikaru themselves, as well as all the faces they met along their adventure.

[b]Characters[/b]

These really are the heart and soul of this VN, which is by design a primarily character-driven and –focused story. And if that’s your jam, I’m very happy to report that it’s with these very characters, their struggles and relationships, that Neko truly shines!

While they do have their exaggerated “anime moments” and some may come across as superficial at first, they eventually all turn out to be deeply layered individuals, to the point of feeling like real people.

This is especially true for our two main characters, Aiko and Hikaru. Their actions and choices may have admittedly infuriated me at times, but not because they were unrealistic or impossible to follow logically. Quite the contrary: they act exactly the way people their ages and with their backgrounds should. Watching both of them grow and the bond between them deepen was a very wholesome and heart-warming experience, even if there were many equally heart-wrenching moments strewn throughout, as they either faced difficult obstacles together or butted heads with each other.

The character writing is definitely what impressed me the most. Well, with one exception that is: the main villain.

While they do get their back story and it’s sufficient enough to understand their motives and actions, I do wish they would have been fleshed out a bit more. It’s precisely because the rest of the cast was handled so superbly that this one sticks out all the more. Although, in the grand scheme of things, it’s still more of a minor complaint to me personally.

It’s easy to overlook, given how attached I have grown to all the other characters.

And it’s because of how intriguing their individual stories and struggles were that I could easily overlook the straightforwardness of the overall plot, too.

[b]Visuals[/b]

These received a lot of care and attention to detail as well. There are tons of very expressive sprites with great variation, ranging from small details (such as injuries) to full-on outfit changes. Heck, even minor characters that only appear briefly get full sprites! It wasn’t necessary to go this far, but it’s very much appreciated!

There is also eye-blinking and a lot of sprite movement going on, giving everything more life rather than too much of a static feel.

Furthermore, you get some neat background variation, a good amount of CGs for important scenes and even a whole bunch of super adorable chibi CGs to keep things visually interesting!

Really, the only problem I have in the visual department are the clashing styles, as the characters in the CGs were drawn by a different artist than those who handled the sprites, resulting in a bit of visual discrepancy. It’s not that anything looks “bad”, but as someone who likes consistency, I do have to admit that this required some getting used to.

[b]Sound[/b]

Maybe a bit more variation would have been nice her as well (there are 19 tracks in total), but what’s there in terms of music is always fitting and very catchy/memorable!

Sound effects were well utilized, sometimes in very clever ways that would make clear what happened without the need of any visuals or text to convey it.

While there is no full voice-acting, you do get occasional soundbytes for most characters, which also help to liven things up.

[b]Gameplay[/b]

It’s a visual novel, so of course, you’ll mostly be reading. That said, there is some interactivity in the form of choices that will affect dialogues, your relationship with some of the characters or your ending (there are a lot of very “fun” bad ends… which definitely didn’t break me… not at all………).

Occasionally, you will also get text input prompts (restricted to one route), which was a nice change of pace, but they occur extremely rarely. Though I rather prefer them being utilized during impactful/sensible moments only, instead of being shoved in just for the sake of it.

[b]Replayability/Dual POV[/b]

This is one of those games where it’s really worth going through twice to experience both perspectives. Hikaru and Aiko actually get separated a lot, resulting in a ton of unique scenes for each route. It felt like there was more variation than overlap and even if the latter did occur, it was still very interesting and fun to hear the differing thoughts of the other protagonist. 

Seriously, this is another area in which Neko really shines, as the dual POV was put to really good use and truly enhances the experience!

[b]Conclusion[/b]

Neko No Sentouki tells a beautiful (sometimes very funny and other times very tragic) story with characters I will never forget and already miss dearly. I really want to see more of them, be it through bonus episodes or a sequel, so please consider giving it a shot yourself!
 
It’s well worth your time and, given the amount of content you’re getting, I’d consider it a steal even at full price!

review:
I will give this game an approve rating, though I will have to discuss this game to a point of being not what it's supposed to be.

Firstly, the game is advertised as anime, and it is not. A cutscene or an option at the beginning does not qualify as anime. If there was going to be usage of AI renderings, I think there were many instances where the game could have used AI-generated walls, AI-generated characters models, and just gone full all-in on the AI-generated content to really see what an AI-animated game could be. There were so many wasted opportunities to be innovated on the AI-generated content front of making an original recipe game that has similarities to dark souls.

Instead, the design is questionable, the levels are short, the monsters are static, and the game story is just cringeworthy. It reminds me of the early 90ies games where everything was so cookie-cutter that the design was stage based, which is this kind of game. It's almost not recommending, but I do think if this was developed by a small team, then it can be promising that the development for these kinds of game may have gotten easier to the point of becoming accessible. The voice acting, while not top tier, still is acceptable to the point of what this game stands to achieve.

Also, playtesting was not conducted on this game properly. Playtesting is a time to really check perimeter barriers, to make sure that players can explore environments correctly, and just ensure that quality assurance was conducted. Some of the levels feel like a mario maker bad-designed level where people could shortcut there way through the stage due to improper level design. If the level isn't functioning properly, that's a huge marker against the game where it was unnecessary.

For the adult category, I think this was a huge missed opportunity. It has nudity, but the nudity feels like it wasn't really a planned objective with this game. There are no erotic scene whatsoever, and the adult-ness becomes kind of put in a pseudo-adult category since if there are clothes on the woman, it would complete censor the game too easily. There were not a real effort to make the game adult and it just lack any sort of bite to make it worth considering as an adult game.

For all intents and purposes, I think the game has the flaws it does and waste a lot of valuable opportunity at demonstrating real AI-generated content for designs in the game, but it still somewhat okay at the point it's at.

review:
UPDATE: Played the game a lot more after reviewing, thought I was mad cuz bad. All my criticisms are the same and also the netcode SUCKS

Steam needs a mixed review option tbh, I don’t want to give this game a full thumbs down but I don’t want to give it a thumbs up either 

AFQM is a nice little platform fighter (without ledges, shields, or grabs, so like Rivals 1) with fun-feeling movement and a couple gimmicks to its name, mainly getting an airdash after getting a hit. This is, in theory, an incredible system, and it feels like crack to get a combo off that uses one cancel, let alone multiple.  Real platfighter heads remember this was the concept of Rushdown Revolution, a truly truly tragic story of a game.

However, that’s also where the issues arise. The game’s movement and overall feel has this weird… sloshy/slippery/unintuitive feeling, and while it’s not a huge issue on its own (plenty of other platfighters have less than stellar gamefeel), the problem arises when you realize the amount of precision the game wants you to have to make the most of its mechanics. Hitboxes are tight and movement is sloshy while the game wants you to be pulling off airdash after airdash mid combo, and while I can’t deny that it’s certainly possible, it absolutely feels out of reach to an average player. I don’t necessarily want to git gud to experience a game’s selling point, especially since I’ve got thousands of platfighter hours behind me.

Part of the issue might also be the characters? Rend is so hilariously slow in both movement and melee that the airdash system doesn’t actually benefit him, plus he feels like ass to play anyway. Knockt is really cool setplay but his melee hitboxes are so precise in both size and timing that you’d have to pull off some Nostradamus tier reads to be able to take advantage of airdashes. Wizard is just Fox with a little setplay and benefits most from the airdash system on account of having the quickest moves in the air alongside some slightly generous hitboxes.

Overall, AFQM is a good game, but unless you want to devote an unreasonable amount of time to learning its overly-stringent ropes, then you’d be better served playing most any other platform fighter. Still, it’s incredibly cheap and at least worth a shot for that alone.

Came here as a melee player, here's my overall thoughts:
(tl;dr get it its worth the 5 bucks easily) 
Punish game: 
Pros: overall very strong due to being able to dash and jump out of aerials upon hit. really fun to use and the hit effects are really good, actually feel the impact (something that most indie platform fighters get wrong in my opinion, ie roa2) 

Cons: my only 2 problems with it are that the damage of moves are not nearly high enough, so you can feel like you had a massive combo but did like 35%, and kill moves aren't strong enough. i feel like they're going to kill, but then they don't. if smash attack knockbacks were increased by 20%, then it would feel really satisfying and logical. if these two problems were fixed, it would be really good.
Neutral: 

Pros: lots of fast, fun movement, especially on eureka (who is kinda like a combination of melee fox and pm lucas). wavedashing is a thing too lol. 

Cons: overall, unfortunately, this is the worst aspect of the game. it feels like you're fishing a lot just to get a hit, since everything combos. adding more defensive options would be really important and make it feel like there's more to it than not getting hit and trying to land a hit. 

Edgeguarding: 

Pros: due to the combo system, you can combo pretty deep offstage which can be really satisfying, makes you work for it too.

Cons: yeah, edgeguarding is ridiculously hard. every stage has wall jumpable walls, which refreshes your up special, you can dash up, wall jump, etc and there's no free fall. out of the 3 characters, 1 can literally teleport across the stage with upspecial, 1 has snake's recovery in smash, and the weakest one gets a massive upwards boost. please nerf recoveries.

Netplay: 

pros: it's good, nothing more to be said.

cons?: lots of people play on bad wifi, so if you could get paired with people in your ping range that would be nice. also, having ranked would be cool.

overall: great game, just please fix the bad stuff i mentioned devs

I was looking forward to this game when I seen HBox play it, the game mechanics are awesome I mean like doing a combo with cancels feels GREAT. Moving around feels very melee, like the big sword character (I forgot the names lol) movements feels like melee falcon so like no complaints on that.

I feel like the biggest thing that this game is missing was an in-game tutorial. With such a unique mechanic as move cancels, I really wanted to learn the new mechanic but then there was no tutorial so like what was I supposed to do? I did training room for like 10 minutes to learn the mechanics and all the 3 characters out. Speaking of like the characters, I feel that there being really no "Jack of all trades" character and that really put me off. I either had to choose from a zoner, combo heavy/tricky character, or a heavy swinger with no fast moves. It made learning the game weird because I couldn't really pay attention to learning the mechanics as a whole, I had to learn the game as "how does my archetype work with the games mechanics." Like this game not having a "Mario" or "Kirby" really sets it back. It's three dramatic renditions of standard stereotypes (as listed above) without a middle ground character. Idk it just seemed strange to me

The game itself like said before, feels great. Wave dashing and moving feel great. Being in an actual match is where all of the mechanics and good things fall apart. Idk if it's me playing on controller or not but attacking felt kind of unresponsive at times. I also tested with multiple controllers and felt the same so it might just be how the game deals with controllers. Anyway, another thing that was weird was teching. I felt like half of the time I was put into hitstun I could tech being hit on the ground but then I would get hit by the same thing and it would just leave me standing looking lost. That whole thing was present in every single match I played. (Again it could of been the controller thing)

All in all, good game it's just that I have my gripes and it makes it feel very clunky imo (except the movement, I really like the movement.) All the things I mentioned were just really taking me out of the game and at some moments just making me question "why didn't that come out?"

Anyway if you enjoy the game, you enjoy the game. I'll probably keep playing it to see how I feel about it. I have high hopes for it and I am happy that it looks like it has a future!!!

review:
Seeing the trailer made me very excited for this game's release, reminding me of my childhood watching all of those stick-fight videos.

However, the game itself does not live up to it so much.
[hr][/hr]
[h1]I: The Controls[/h1]
Coming from someone who's played a couple of platform fighters in the past (Primarily Smash Bros.), the controls are very clunky and your character feels like it's in constant hitstun-- even when you're just moving around normally. I got to admit, the air-dashing aspect of the game feels unique and a breath of fresh air, opening up many different strange combo routes and mixups to combat DI.

Sadly, it doesn't seem like this game has native Gamecube support (among other supports that may/may not work) and that's my personal dig with it. I even tried hooking up a third-party USB-3.0 Gamecube controller and that didn't work either, with that I had to go through Steam's way of using their controller support and then my inputs ended up being either double-tapped or not tapped at all.
[hr][/hr]
[h1]II: The Gameplay (And learning curve)[/h1]
Even with a lot of experience with platfighters, three words came to mind.
[b][i]"Where's the tutorial?"[/i][/b]

Not only is there no tutorial, there's no moves list, it's completely unintuitive to people who have never played a platform fighter before and, repeating as before, it's really clunky. The "smooth-flowing combos" shown in trailer have very tight controls to pull off even remotely consistently, and the launching mechanics make you feel like you can't do anything out of disadvantage. Which you really can't, besides parry. And that only works on the ground-- good luck getting out of any aerial combos.

Speaking of very tight controls, the learning curve feels way too tight. It took me maybe 10 minutes to figure out how to actually hit half of the moves of the characters due to the odd and clunky frame data, and utilizing them in combos is quite difficult for the fast-paced nature of the game.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]TLDR: It's aight.[/h2]
I can feel that the game itself has a lot of heart and energy put into it, but it simply feels too unpolished for a full release like this. There's no tutorial, no information on how the controls and character function, and the contrast between the speedy nature of the game and the sloth-like and jittery movement still feel very odd to play with. And the disadvantage state in this game is completely awful, with little to no ways to get out of combos (especially in the air) and only having to rely on DI.

Text wall over, hit the game with some high-grit sandpaper and loosen up the controls and I'd say it's pretty a solid start to what feels like a good platform fighter. [b]4/10 i'd say at least try it out[/b]

Atm gotta give this a negative review. I was really looking forward to this game because the style has a certain charm to it, but the menu is HELL to navigate. I'm not sure who thought it was smart to ship the game with these menu controls, but here's the rundown:

Most video games follow the same default button mapping, such as: "ESC" for menu or pause, "E" to pickup, "Shift" to sprint, "Ctrl" to crouch.... You get the point. Somehow, the devs here thought it would be a smart idea to reinvent the default buttons. "Backspace" is used to go back in the menu, "Enter" is used to pause in a match, however "Enter" is also used to confirm things, but so can "Space", however it's random on which one works when. There IS a cursor, but only during character selection, and even then it can only be controlled using the arrow keys... I don't know much about game deving, but is that not more work than just mapping the cursor to mouse movement?

You also cannot rebind the menu navigation buttons, and attempting to rebind the Pause button from "Enter" to "ESC" just cancels out of the bind procedure, so it's impossible to do. Being able to change binds in training should also be possible. You shouldn't have to exit out into the main menu just to tweak one button to see how it feels in game.

Selecting your custom button mapping is also hidden under a random pop up menu under your character AFTER having selected them, the game does not explain this to you at all.

Please devs, just be normal and 1. Add a usable MOUSE cursor on the menu. 2. Remap the default menu buttons to what they are in like every modern major game, if someone wants to use backspace instead of esc, let them map it to that themselves? 3. Add rebinding during training, already explained this above. 4. Make it a little more obvious for players on how to actually select and use their remapped controls.

I wont refund yet, Pluto did answer me in the Discord server and mentioned that the menu and UI will get updated after a week or so. REALLY really looking forward to that and hoping that word is kept. I also apologise for being harsh in my review, but I also do not understand how any of these choices were okay'd for release.

review:
i feel like a lot of the initial hype on this game comes from people who haven't played a lot of platform fighters outside of smash and rivals and are really quickly impressed by having something that seems "unique" and has a nice art style, but when looking deepers the problems quickly begin to show in this game

i'm gonna start with the hitboxes, weird and inconsistent knockback/hitstun and how slow this makes the game feel despite advertising itself as flashy. oh my god why are the hitboxes in this game so damn tiny? this combined with the fact that everything is also incredibly safe - even parry honestly - makes it a way more defensive game when played optimally than it initally seems, because small hitboxes + low landing lag = hit punishing feels almost impossible when players know how to space properly

not to mention that when you do get a hit, sometimes the knockback or hitstun just feels wayyyy too low? it's super inconsistent too;  for some reason knockt's mine does way more knockback when someone is on the ground than versus someone is in the air

all of this leads to this game being super super prone to very campy gameplay and once people stop drooling over the allegedly "unique" core combo mechanic that was taken 1 to 1 from rushdown revolt and start being bored by it, the game willl almost certainly devolve into this kind of super defensive gameplay. despite winning most of my matches, a lot of them almost went to time.

not to mention the characters themselves... i just don't think they're unique at all. knockt is almost exactly fleet and just doesn't feel very satisfying to play and doesn't interact much with the core mechanics of the game, rend feels like brawlhalla greatsword + cloud but actualy way less fun to play than either (the most useless shorthop button ive ever seen on any character), and eureka is just fox + falcon with worse feeling buttons than both.


i don't see what makes this game unique, not even its stickman aesthetic is that novel to me.
it's not that original, and it also just doesn't feel very good to control. something about the ground movement just feels horrendous to me, super clunky (and i've played almost every notable title in this genre lol)

i wish i had much positive to say about it besides maybe the price, but as of right now it's an incredibly middling experience that feels more enjoyable to watch "hype clips" of than actually play
